title: AI-Driven Risk Management and Energy Supply Chain Resilience: The Moderating Role of Supply Chain Complexity
summary: This study examines the association between AI-driven risk management and energy supply chain resilience in Jordan, with supply chain complexity incorporated as a moderating variable.Grounded in dynamic capabilities theory, the study adopts a quantitative, cross-sectional design and draws on survey data collected from 248 supply chain, operations, risk management, and digital transformation professionals in Jordan's energy sector.Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the hypothesized direct and moderating effects.The findings indicate a statistically significant positive association between AI-driven risk management and energy supply chain resilience, while supply chain complexity is found to significantly moderate this relationship, suggesting that the strength of the association varies across different levels of structural complexity within the supply chain.These results provide empirical evidence of a relationship between AIdriven capabilities and resilience outcomes in an emerging economy context and should be interpreted as associative rather than causal, given the cross-sectional research design.The study contributes to the logistics and informatics literature by offering sector-specific insights from Jordan's energy supply chain, where digital infrastructure and data-driven coordination mechanisms are still developing.

title: The Impacts of Product Architecture and Logistics Techniques on Supply Chain Resilience and Ripple Effect
summary: Background: Supply chain (SC) ability to recover from disruption (i.e., resilience) is vital for thriving businesses, thus its relevance. This study investigates how resilience to disruption and disruption propagation (i.e., ripple effect (RE)) are influenced by product architecture (PA) and logistics strategies. Methods: Four SC configurations, derived from structural combinations of PA (integral and modular) with two logistics techniques (inventory storage and cross-docking), were generated using discrete-event simulation in FlexSim. Each SC configuration was subjected to five scenarios: no disruption; isolated disruptions at the distribution center (DC) and at the manufacturer; simultaneous disruptions; and sequential disruptions. Results: The results indicated a smoother recovery and lower post-disruption back-order rates for modular PA than for integral PA. Inventory buffering was higher in SC networks with DC storage than in those with cross-docking. The study found increased downstream and upstream disruption propagation under sequential disruptions, illustrating RE. Conclusions: The study suggests that integrating PA with logistics strategies early in supply chain design may improve recovery and overall supply chain performance.

title: CSR officers as heterodox brokers in Kanaky New Caledonia: Travelling models and spatialising effects
summary: Abstract Nickel extraction and processing have profoundly shaped Kanaky New Caledonia's social, political and colonial/decolonial trajectory over the past 150 years. This activity has transformed material and mental landscapes while generating intermediary officers whose roles evolved over time. Since the 2000s, the arrival of transnational corporations introduced ‘travelling models’, such as impact and benefit agreements (IBA), corporate social responsibility (CSR) and social licence to operate (SLO), which mediate global discourses and reshape local arenas. This paper focuses on CSR officers as development brokers, a relatively unexplored theme in CSR and mining anthropology. It advances two hypotheses: first, CSR officers differ from traditional brokers by structurally working toward corporate local anchoring (or ‘social acceptability’) and brokering not only development but also compensation, social peace and institutional design, thus also endorsing a diplomatic role; second, they contribute to defining mining impact and influence perimeters and arenas at both local and New Caledonian levels. Drawing on research conducted between 2008 and 2022, particularly the social biographies of CSR officers across firms and sectors, the analysis highlights the spatialising effects of brokerage and strategic role in transforming minescapes.

title: Dampak Penerbitan Green Bonds dan Green Innovation terhadap Nilai Perusahaan di Indonesia
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of Green Bonds and Green Innovation on Firm Value among public companies in Indonesia during the 2019-2024 period. The research employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and other supporting sources. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 28 companies with 168 observations. Green Bonds are measured using a dummy variable, while Green Innovation is measured through a disclosure index based on GRI 302, GRI 303, GRI 305, and GRI 306. Firm Value is proxied by Tobin’s Q. Data analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model (REM), which was selected based on panel model testing. The results show that Green Bonds do not have a significant effect on Firm Value. Similarly, Green Innovation does not significantly affect Firm Value. These findings indicate that green financing instruments and environmental disclosure practices have not yet become major considerations for investors in assessing company value in the Indonesian capital market. The results also suggest that investors tend to place greater emphasis on financial performance and other fundamental factors when making investment decisions. Furthermore, the low coefficient of determination indicates that Firm Value is influenced by many factors beyond those included in this study. This research contributes to the sustainable finance literature by providing empirical evidence that the implementation of green financing and environmental sustainability practices does not necessarily generate a direct positive market response in developing countries.

title: Green Finance: From a Fragmented Literature to an Integrated Conceptual Framework
summary: Green finance has emerged as an important field of research and policy but remains conceptually diverse, particularly in relation to sustainable finance and related concepts. This study systematically examines the evolution and conceptual structure of the green finance literature and develops an integrated conceptual framework for green finance. The research design involves a three-stage workflow combining bibliometric mapping of 10,662 Web of Science and Scopus publications, a multi-criteria Article Relevance Index (ARI) for article selection, and qualitative full-text analysis of 209 articles supported by AI-assisted extraction and researcher validation. The bibliometric analysis reveals a rapidly expanding but conceptually fragmented field, with 94% of occurrences of 15 representative author keywords concentrated in 2020–2026. Full-text analysis identifies five interrelated defining attributes of green finance. The results show that green finance occupies a distinct position within the broader sustainable finance domain, with green financing as its narrower operational component, while climate finance and ESG finance remain related but distinct concepts. These findings are integrated into a conceptual framework that represents green finance as an interconnected system of defining attributes, conceptual relationships, and boundaries, supporting more consistent interpretation and future operationalization.

title: GATT 1994 and the Agreement on Agriculture on Global Food Security: Rethinking Export Restrictions and Supply Chains Resilience
summary: Global food security relies heavily on resilient, efficient supply chains to facilitate cross-border agricultural trade. However, export restrictions and prohibitions implemented by World Trade Organization (WTO) Members to safeguard domestic supplies frequently disrupt global markets, disproportionately harming net food-importing nations. This article examines the extent to which WTO law, specifically the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) 1994 and the Agreement on Agriculture (AoA), impacts global food security and supply chain resilience. This article employs doctrinal legal analysis to examine GATT Article XI and Article 12 of the AoA. The findings reveal that GATT Article XI:2(a) affords excessive policy discretion; key legal thresholds such as "essential products" and "critical shortages" lack precise definitions, and the provision fails to impose clear time limits on restrictive measures. Furthermore, Article 12 of the AoA provides limited discipline because notification, consultation, and food-security considerations lack effective enforcement mechanisms. This regulatory flexibility increases uncertainty in international markets and vulnerability among food-importing countries. The article therefore proposes reforms introducing clearer criteria, transparency obligations, proportionality requirements, and duration limits for export measures. Balancing necessary domestic policy space during genuine crises with tighter multilateral disciplines will reinforce supply chain resilience and solidify the role of international agricultural trade in safeguarding global food security.

title: Audit Committee Expertise and Earnings Management in South Africa: The Moderating Role of Audit Quality
summary: This study examines the moderating effect of audit quality (AQ) on the relationship between audit committee expertise (ACE) and earnings management (EM). A quantitative approach was used to investigate 128 non-financial companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) from 2021 to 2025. The data collection sources included annual reports, the Osiris database, and the Who Owns Whom database. ACE was measured using audit committee financial expertise (ACFE), educational level expertise (ACEL), and industry expertise (ACIE). AQ was proxied by a dummy variable equal to 1 if the audit was conducted by a Big 4 audit firm (BIG4), and 0 otherwise. EM proxies included accrual earnings management (AEM) and real earnings management (REM). The fixed effects model (FEM) was used to test the hypotheses. The FEM regression results without a moderating variable indicate that ACFE has an insignificant positive impact on AEM and REM. ACEL has an insignificant negative impact on AEM, while a significant positive impact on REM. However, ACIE has a significant negative impact on AEM, while a significant positive impact on REM. On the other hand, the FEM regression results with a moderating variable indicate that the interaction of BIG4*ACFE has an insignificant negative impact on AEM, while a significant negative impact on REM. Yet BIG4*ACEL has an insignificant positive impact on AEM, while an insignificant positive impact on REM. Yet, the interaction of BIG4*ACIE has a significant negative impact on AEM, while a significant positive impact on REM. The results highlight that non-financial companies listed on the JSE should not presume that any single type of ACE will mitigate all forms of EM. This research enriches the existing corporate governance literature by providing comprehensive insights into the relationship between ACE and EM proxies, moderated by AQ proxied by Big 4 audit firms.

title: The Role of Big Data and AI In Capital Market Based Accounting
summary: This study used a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to examine the role and use of Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in capital market-based accounting and identify factors influencing the effectiveness of their implementation. The study followed the PRISMA 2020 protocol. From 437 records obtained through eight keyword combinations in the Scopus database, 29 studies were selected after filtering based on the 2016–2026 publication period, Q1–Q4 journal quality, and thematic relevance. The study grouped the literature into four main aspects: data infrastructure, analytical processing, disclosure and reporting, and governance and assurance. These four aspects were then integrated into the AI-Accounting Value Chain and Governance Loop (AVC-GL) model. The findings indicate that Big Data expands information sources for accounting and capital market analysis, while AI helps process complex data and supports decision-making. However, the effectiveness of its implementation is highly dependent on data quality, governance, professional oversight, and human ability to evaluate technological outcomes. The use of generative AI also improves the efficiency of corporate disclosures, but introduces new risks, including greenwashing. This study contributes through the development of a functional taxonomy and AVC-GL model to explain the relationship between technology, governance, information quality, and decision-making in capital markets.

title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY AND THE ECONOMIC SECURITY OF POLISH BUSINESSES: RISK REDUCTION MECHANISMS AND A STRUCTURAL-FUNCTIONAL MODEL
summary: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) increasingly shapes how enterprises manage resource dependence, workforce continuity, stakeholder relationships, and exposure to environmental and regulatory risks. For Polish businesses, these issues are particularly relevant amid high energy costs, shortages of skilled employees, and disruptions to supply chains. This study aims to explain how CSR may influence enterprise economic security and to develop a framework for assessing the relevant risk-reduction mechanisms. The research examines the economic security of enterprises operating in Poland, with a focus on the relationship between responsible business practices and financial, operational, human capital, market-reputational, and institutional security. The study combines stakeholder theory with systemic, structural-functional, and risk-oriented approaches. It applies comparative document analysis and descriptive analysis to published Polish enterprise statistics and the 2025 European Investment Bank Investment Survey; it does not treat datasets with different populations as a single firm-level sample. Among Polish firms surveyed in 2025, 94% reported measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, 63% conducted energy audits, and 45% set emissions targets. At the same time, 64% reported exposure to physical climate risks, while 46% implemented climate adaptation measures; 86% identified energy costs and 81% the availability of skilled staff as investment obstacles. Statistics Poland reported that net turnover profitability among the non-financial enterprises covered by its surveys rose from 3.4% in 2024 to 3.7% in 2025. These indicators describe CSR-related practices and economic conditions but do not establish that CSR caused the change in profitability. The study proposes an original definition of CSR-oriented economic security and develops a five-dimensional structural-functional model. It links responsible resource use, workforce development, supplier due diligence, stakeholder dialogue, and transparent governance to potential reductions in financial, operational, personnel, market, and compliance vulnerabilities. The model's practical value lies in helping managers select CSR measures according to material economic risks and evaluate them using observable cost, continuity, staffing, and compliance indicators. Future firm-level research should test the proposed relationships while accounting for enterprise size, sector, and initial financial condition.

title: CEO Inherited Altruism, Firm Corporate Social Responsibility, and Shareholder Returns
summary: Abstract We examine the impact of CEOs’ inherited altruistic inclination on firm corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance and shareholder returns. Specifically, we look at U.S. CEOs’ altruism as an inherited value of the CEOs’ ancestral cultural origin that shapes their moral behavior and influences firm commitment to altruistic and genuine CSR. We find that firms led by CEOs with stronger inherited altruistic preferences have better CSR performance after controlling for firm financial and corporate governance attributes and other leadership characteristics. The impact of CEO inherited altruism on CSR is higher when CEOs operate under lower cash flow pressure. Consistent with a view of ethical leadership which protects the interests of both stakeholders and shareholders, we find that CEOs who inherit altruistic preferences are not significantly associated with firms’ stock returns under normal circumstances, while they protect shareholder returns during times of financial crisis and recessions. The results survive several robustness and endogeneity checks.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE IN THE IT DECISION-MAKING SYSTEM OF BANKING INSTITUTIONS UNDER DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
summary: The article examines the role of corporate governance in the IT decision-making system of banking institutions under the digital transformation of entrepreneurial structures. The relevance of the study is determined by the changing role of information technologies, which contribute to the automation and continuity of operational processes while simultaneously providing the foundation for innovation, business model transformation, the development of digital customer interaction channels, and risk management. The purpose of the article is to develop a theoretical and methodological basis for substantiating the role of corporate governance in the IT decision-making system of banking institutions and to develop a conceptual approach to their integrated IT management in interaction with entrepreneurial structures. The object of the study is the processes of corporate and IT management in banking institutions under digital transformation, while the subject comprises the interrelationships and mechanisms underlying the formulation and adoption of IT decisions. The study employs systemic, strategic, process-oriented, and risk-oriented approaches, as well as the methods of analysis, synthesis, comparison, generalization, and structural-logical modelling. The article substantiates the dichotomous role of information technologies in banking activities and the need to move from fragmented IT project management to systemic management of technological development. The IT decision-making system is improved by identifying a set of interrelated stages. A concept of integrated IT management is proposed that combines corporate strategy, digital strategy, corporate governance, IT management, business needs, technological capabilities, resources, and risks into a single management cycle with a feedback mechanism. Statistical data confirm the scale of digitalization of banking operations and their direct relationship with the functioning of entrepreneurial structures, particularly trade enterprises. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of applying the proposed approach to align corporate and digital strategies, substantiate IT decisions, manage technological risks, and develop information technology management systems in other entrepreneurial structures.

title: Does Corporate Governance Matter for Accounting Conservatism?
summary: The relationship between firm size, leverage, and accounting conservatism is explored in this paper, using independent commissioners as a moderating variable. A sample consisting of 22 mining and energy enterprises listed on the IDX was established through purposive sampling. For hypotheses testing, this research utilizes multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The data analysis indicates that leverage negatively and significantly influences accounting conservatism, while firm size yields a significant positive outcome. Regarding the moderating mechanism, independent commissioners show no capacity to moderate the leverage-conservatism link, yet they markedly weaken the impact of firm size on accounting conservatism. This finding highlights that proper governance through independent commissioners elevates the reliability of financial disclosures, making excessive accounting conservatism less necessary for large corporations.

title: Pengungkapan Corporate Social Responsibility Berbasis Tri Hita Karana terhadap Nilai Perusahaan dengan Good Corporate Governance sebagai Variabel Moderasi
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of Tri Hita Karana-based Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosure on firm value, the effect of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) on firm value, and the role of GCG in moderating the relationship between Tri Hita Karana-based CSR and firm value. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey method. The research population consisted of all 30 employees of Villa Bugis, and the entire population was used as the sample through a saturated sampling technique. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using validity tests, reliability tests, multiple linear regression analysis, and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with the assistance of SPSS software. The results indicate that Tri Hita Karana-based Corporate Social Responsibility has a positive and significant effect on firm value. Good Corporate Governance also has a positive and significant effect on firm value. However, Good Corporate Governance is unable to moderate the relationship between Tri Hita Karana-based Corporate Social Responsibility and firm value. The findings suggest that the implementation of CSR based on local wisdom values and the application of Good Corporate Governance can enhance firm value.

title: Audit Opinions and Earnings Management: Evidence from Listed Firms in Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE)
summary: Background: Financial reports can be distorted by financial earnings management, which lowers their transparency and dependability. Consequently, it continues to be a major issue in financial reporting. By offering an impartial evaluation of financial statements, audits contribute to accurate reporting, and audit opinions strengthen managerial responsibility for the caliber of financial reporting. Objectives: This research aims to probe the relationship between audit opinions and the earning management practiced by the KLSE's public companies. It In particular checks if the public companies with modified audit opinions have a different way of managing earnings from those of the firms with unmodified audit opinions, that is, clean ones. Methods: This research uses a quantitative design based on panel data collected from KLSE-listed companies' annual reports and online databases. The sample comprises 665 firm-year observations over the period 2017–2021. To analyze the relationship between audit opinions and earnings management, various statistical tests were conducted. Results: The findings indicate that Auditor Opinion is negatively and significantly associated with Earnings Management. This finding suggests that firms receiving more rigorous and skeptical audit opinions are associated with lower levels of earnings management. Conclusion: The findings indicate that Auditor Opinion is negatively and significantly associated with Earnings Management. This negative association provides evidence of a significant relationship between audit opinions and financial reporting quality. The findings may assist investors, regulators, auditors, and other stakeholders in assessing corporate reporting practices and financial transparency.

title: Internal Audit Quality and Green Lending: Strengthening Low-Carbon Environmental Performance in Indonesian Listed Commercial Banks
summary: The transition toward a low-carbon economy has increased the importance of sustainable finance and effective corporate governance within the banking industry. Green lending has become a key financing strategy for supporting environmentally sustainable investments; however, prior studies have largely examined internal governance and green lending separately, leaving limited evidence on whether Internal Audit Quality can strengthen the environmental effects of green lending. This study examines the effects of Internal Audit Quality (IAQ) and Green Lending (GL) on Low-Carbon Environmental Performance (LCEP) and investigates whether IAQ strengthens the relationship between GL and LCEP in Indonesian listed commercial banks. Using a quantitative research design, this study analyzes panel data from 47 Indonesian listed commercial banks during 2020–2024, resulting in 235 firm-year observations. The hypotheses are tested using a Fixed Effect Model (FEM) following panel model selection tests. IAQ is measured using a disclosure-based index, GL is measured by the proportion of green financing, and LCEP is measured using a composite disclosure index reflecting banks’ environmental commitments and low-carbon initiatives. The results indicate that IAQ has a positive and significant effect on LCEP (β = 0.367, p = 0.0001), while GL also has a positive and significant effect on LCEP (β = 0.298, p = 0.0002). Furthermore, the interaction between IAQ and GL is positive and significant (β = 0.184, p = 0.0061), indicating that higher IAQ strengthens the positive effect of GL on LCEP. These findings highlight the strategic role of internal auditing in strengthening governance and supporting sustainable finance implementation. The study contributes to the sustainable finance and corporate governance literature by integrating IAQ and GL within a unified framework to explain LCEP in emerging-market banking institutions.

title: Toward a Sharia-Based Ecological Accounting Framework: Integrating Environmental Cost Recognition with Islamic Environmental Jurisprudence
summary: This study reconstructs ecological accounting by addressing a critical gap in sustainability accounting: existing CSR and ESG disclosures often report environmental responsibility without recognizing ecological degradation as a measurable corporate obligation. The study integrates environmental cost accounting with Islamic environmental jurisprudence to develop a Sharia-based ecological accounting framework for sustainable corporate governance. Methodologically, it combines bibliometric mapping, critical literature synthesis, semi-structured interviews with twelve experts, grounded theory coding, and expert validation. The bibliometric analysis reveals weak intellectual integration among sustainability accounting, ecological economics, and Islamic environmental governance. Interview findings reveal that CSR practices are often symbolic, with ecological costs are externalized to communities, ecosystems, and future generations. The proposed framework operationalizes ecological accountability through five components: ecological cost recognition, Sharia-based ethical classification, governance integration, reporting and disclosure mechanisms, and assurance and verification procedures. This study contributes by shifting Islamic sustainability accounting from ethical disclosure toward cost-based, auditable, and governance-oriented ecological accountability.

title: Integration of Strategic CSR and Digital Leadership to Supply Chain Sustainability in Jordanian Public Hospitals: Moderating Role of Green Technology and E-Knowledge Sharing
summary: The aim of this study was to analyze the effect of strategic corporate social responsibility and digital leadership on supply chain sustainability in Jordanian public hospitals.It also examined the moderating effects of green technology and e-knowledge sharing in these relationships.The study population consisted of public hospitals in Jordan, including Ministry of Health hospitals, military hospitals, and university hospitals.A stratified sampling technique was applied to reflect the structure of the Jordanian public healthcare system.Data were collected through an online questionnaire distributed via official e-mail and administrative communication channels.A total of 370 valid responses were obtained from employees working in supply chain, procurement, logistics, pharmacy, and quality management departments.The questionnaire items were measured using a five-point Likert scale, and the data were analyzed using SmartPLS.The findings indicate that strategic corporate social responsibility has a positive and significant effect on supply chain sustainability.Digital leadership also has a positive and significant effect on supply chain sustainability.The results further show that green technology positively and significantly moderates the relationship between strategic corporate social responsibility and supply chain sustainability, as well as the relationship between digital leadership and supply chain sustainability.However, e-knowledge sharing does not significantly moderate the relationship between strategic corporate social responsibility and supply chain sustainability.The moderating effect of e-knowledge sharing on the relationship between digital leadership and supply chain sustainability was not retained in the final interpretation due to concerns regarding an unusually large initial interaction coefficient requiring further robustness verification.Based on these findings, the study emphasizes the importance of aligning responsible strategic practices, digital leadership capabilities, and green technology adoption to support sustainable supply chain practices in Jordanian public hospitals.The study recommends strengthening digital leadership competencies, encouraging the adoption of green technologies, and developing structured digital knowledge-sharing mechanisms to enhance the resilience and sustainability of healthcare supply chains in Jordanian public hospitals.

title: Spirituality Accounting and Fair Value Financial Reporting
summary: Accounting for spirituality and fair value reporting in Nigeria are being studied in this study. This study utilized a survey research design. Public officials from the South-South States of Nigeria make up the bulk of the study's population. Data gathering for the study was based on primary sources. We utilized descriptive statistics (univariate analysis) to examine the connection between Trustworthiness, Reliability, and Transparency. Results of Bivariate Analysis using Pearson. There is a substantial association between the examined variable and the trustworthiness, reliability, and transparency markers, as shown by the correlation coefficient. Spirituality accounting is strongly related to fair value reporting, according to the study. Appropriate financial information that could plausibly affect the comprehension of financial reports by their intended consumers should be made available by accountants, according to the recommendations. In order to provide employees with a well-rounded understanding, it is important to convey spiritual principles directly during the hiring process. When compiling financial reports, accountants should act in accordance with their moral compass. Organizations need to take spiritual values into consideration if they want to survive in the new economy. Providing employees with meaningful work and valuing their abilities are key components of spiritual accounting. Any company serious about its spiritual mission should encourage and support staff members to express their individuality and creativity. When compiling financial reports, accountants should do so with integrity. The accounting curriculums at the college level need to contain spirituality accounting so that the students who are going to become financial managers upon graduation are cognizant of their spirituality.

title: Business Logic as an Integrated Corporate Governance Mechanism under Uncertainty
summary: Contemporary corporate governance operates in an environment shaped by digital transformation, geopolitical instability, increasing uncertainty, and stronger expectations regarding transparency and stakeholder accountability. These conditions require an integrated approach that connects strategic decision-making, stakeholder interests, risk management, and long-term value creation. This study aims to develop a conceptual model of business logic as an integrated corporate governance mechanism under uncertainty and to determine its theoretical foundations, structural dimensions, and practical significance. The methodology is based on an interdisciplinary theoretical framework combining stakeholder theory, institutional theory, dynamic capabilities, systems thinking, and contemporary corporate governance principles. The study applies analysis and synthesis to generalize existing approaches, comparative analysis to identify their limitations, and conceptual modelling to construct an original three-dimensional framework. The results define business logic as an integrated system of principles, patterns, and managerial mechanisms that aligns stakeholder interests, organizational resources, and external environmental requirements in strategic decision-making. The proposed model integrates three interrelated dimensions, namely managerial, stakeholder, and value dimensions, across six sequential phases of corporate transformation: entropy, nonlinear transformation, divergence, bifurcation, convergence, and formation of a new system. The model links strategic adaptation with risk management, stakeholder engagement, ESG principles, and corporate value creation. Its practical application can support the transition from reactive to preventive risk management, strengthen organizational adaptability and stakeholder trust, and improve the consistency of corporate decisions under uncertainty. The study concludes that business logic can serve as a theoretical and practical framework for continuous corporate transformation. Further research should empirically test the model across industries and develop indicators for assessing transformation phases and their effects on organizational resilience, governance effectiveness, and long-term corporate value.

title: Forensic Accounting and Integrated Financial Reporting of Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
summary: Forensic as accounting is the practice of applying accounting, auditing and investigative talents to detect and explore fraud and other financial misrepresentations in court proceedings. Forensic accounting specialization of accounting that focuses on scrutinizing financial data to find evidence of financial crimes such as fraud, embezzlement and corruption. The study examined forensic accounting and integrated financial reporting of deposit money banks in Nigeria. Specifically, the study examined the effect of risk assessment, legal service, fraud detection, monitoring and control on integrated financial reporting of deposit money banks in Nigeria. The data for this study were obtained from secondary source. Data were collated from a sampled of 10 banks’ annual financial reports and analyzed using both descriptive statistics, Pearson Correlation Matrix and Hausman Effect Test. The result of the study revealed that risk assessment, legal service, monitoring and control had positive effect on integrated financial reporting of deposit money banks in Nigeria which is statistically significant at 5% level of significance. The study concluded that forensic accounting has positive effect on integrated financial reporting of deposit money banks in Nigeria and have improved integrated financial reporting of deposit money banks in Nigeria. The study recommended that management of listed deposit money banks should establish forensic accounting department in each of their branch to enhance the investigative aspect of accounting in deposit money banks in Nigeria. Management of deposit money banks should organize training programme on forensic accounting for the accountants to undergo to refresh their knowledge on forensic accounting so that they can be in position to offer sound advice that can be useful to banks.

title: ESG Disclosure and Audit Quality: A Comparison of the Association Between ESG Ratings and Sustainability Reports with Audit Quality
summary: This study empirically analyzes how corporate sustainability activities—measured by ESG ratings and sustainability report publication—affect audit quality. While prior studies have primarily focused on the relationship between ESG (or CSR) and firm value or financial performance, relatively little attention has been paid to how different forms of ESG information influence audit quality. In particular, few studies distinguish between ESG ratings and sustainability report publication despite their different informational characteristics. Thus, we examine the distinct impacts of ESG ratings and report issuance on audit quality. Research Methods: Using 2,461 KOSPI-listed firm-year observations (2019–2024), we perform multiple and logistic regression analyses. Audit fees, audit hours, and Big 4 auditor selection serve as proxies for audit quality. Propensity Score Matching (PSM) is also utilized to ensure the robustness of our findings. Results in Research: ESG ratings and sustainability report publication are positively associated with audit fees, audit hours, and Big 4 auditor selection. The sustainability report results remain robust after PSM. Research Conclusion: Unlike prior studies treating ESG as a single construct, this study distinguishes ESG ratings from sustainability report publication and demonstrates that each has a significant yet distinct association with audit quality.

title: An exploratory study of supply chain performance in the digital era: evidence from Morocco
summary: This study aims to explore the determinants of supply chain performance in the digital era, with a particular focus on identifying both the benefits and challenges of digital transformation within the Moroccan context. The research seeks to contribute to the understanding of how digital technologies reshape supply chain practices in emerging economies. A qualitative approach was adopted, involving semi-structured interviews with 30 experts and specialists in supply chain management and digital transformation. The collected data were analyzed using a textometric approach, which enabled the identification of recurrent themes, patterns, and relationships among the determinants influencing supply chain performance. The results reveal that digitalization enhances supply chain performance through improved transparency, agility, and cost efficiency, while also fostering stronger collaboration across stakeholders. However, significant challenges persist, including digital infrastructure limitations, high implementation costs, resistance to change, and gaps in digital skills. These findings underscore the dual nature of digital transformation as both an opportunity and a constraint in the Moroccan supply chain landscape. The study provides insights for policymakers and managers to design strategies that leverage digital tools for supply chain optimization while addressing the contextual challenges faced by Moroccan firms. By focusing on Morocco as an emerging economy, this research offers fresh evidence on the role of digital transformation in supply chain performance, contributing to both academic debates and managerial practices in developing contexts.

title: Enhancing Economic Performance in Maritime Transportation via Strategic Partnerships: Empirical Insights from SEM-DEA Hybrid Modelling in an Emerging Market
summary: This study investigates the determinants of supply chain efficiency in maritime transportation enterprises confronting persistent volatility in marine fuel prices and identifies optimal strategic alliance partners. Drawing on strategic alliance theory and supply chain management principles, it develops a relational network model that positions strategic alliance intensity as the central moderator among digital transformation capability, supply chain integration, supply chain resilience and risk management capability, green logistics and environmental compliance, and operational and asset management capability, all converging on supply chain efficiency. Structural equation modelling of survey data reveals that operational and asset management capability exerts the sole substantive direct positive effect on supply chain efficiency (β = 0.47), with the remaining antecedents influencing the outcome primarily through mediated pathways. Input-oriented super slack-based measure data envelopment analysis under variable returns to scale, applied to 2025 audited financial statements, constructs virtual composite decision-making units and identifies the alliance between the Hanoi-based container specialist (DMU10) and the Da Nang-based bulk operator (DMU8) configuration yielding maximal efficiency gains. Theoretically, the research clarifies mediated relational pathways in capital-intensive logistics. Practically, it provides executives and policymakers with a replicable toolkit for partner selection that may help mitigate fuel-price exposure, support decarbonization, and strengthen resilience.

title: Audit Quality and Earnings Management of Listed Non-Financial Firms in Nigeria: The Moderating Role of Board Gender Diversity
summary: The global financial scandal poses great challenge to the credibility and value relevance of the audit function. The consequence of poor external audit in most cases manifest in financial scandals and failure of companies. The main objective of this study was to examine the effect of audit quality on earnings management of listed non-financial firms in Nigeria. The independent variable being audit quality was proxied by audit fees, audit firm size and audit firm tenure while the dependent variable being earnings management was proxied by Modified Jones discretionary accruals. The moderating variable was Board gender diversity. The research design adopted in this study was ex post facto, secondary data were used and the population of study was 100 listed industrial goods companies in Nigeria and 64 were purposively selected as the sample size. The data were analyzed using pooled ordinary least square regression and the statistical package employed was STATA 17. The result of the analysis revealed that Audit fees (coeff = -0.110[0.032]) have a significant negative effect; audit firm size (coeff. = -0.105 [0.022]) has a significant negative effect; audit tenure (coeff. = -0.000 [0.889]) has no significant effect; a ) However, its interaction with audit tenure, audit committee meeting frequency, and auditor’s opinion type was not significant. It was thus concluded that audit quality plays significant role in checkmating earnings management practices with board diversity strengthening this relationship. Based on these findings, it was recommended amongst others that the management of non-financial firms should engage reputable audit firms and be willing to pay adequate audit fees to ensure high-quality audits, preferably those with strong reputational standing such as the Big Four, since their broader expertise and resources contribute to more effective financial reporting oversight.

title: Integrating resilience and sustainability in supply chains: a strategic evaluation framework
summary: Over recent years, global supply chains have been and continue to be under significant pressure resulting from major disruptions largely driven by the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic, persistent geopolitical instability. Supply chains are also increasingly asked to undergo structural transformations to comply with rising sustainability requirements due to accelerating impacts of climate change. Although resilience and sustainability in supply chain and logistics have been largely studied, existing research mainly addresses the two concepts separately and offers limited frameworks to evaluate their simultaneous effects on logistics decision levels. This article proposes an evaluation framework to assess the joint impact of sustainability and resilience practices within organisations’ supply chains. A dual methodological approach is adopted, combining a quantitative literature review using bibliometric analysis (Bibliometrix, Scopus database, 65 selected publications) with a qualitative content review of existing frameworks. Key supply chain practices are identified and classified across strategic, tactical, and operational decision levels, and their cross-impacts are evaluated on resilience and sustainability. The results reveal a structural pattern: Strong synergies between resilience and sustainability arise from practices optimising information flows, collaborative practices with stakeholders, circular and efficiency-driven processes. However, some unavoidable trade-offs are identified such as network diversification and multi-sourcing, inventory buffering, material-flow redundancy strategies and just-in-time management, which enhance resilience but increase resource consumption and transport emissions.The proposed framework offers a cross-impact evaluation tool for managers to assess supply chain resilience and sustainability performance within their organisations and prioritise implementation of strong synergy practices while mitigating trade-offs.

title: Peran Good Corporate Governance dalam Hubungan Profitabilitas, Risiko, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap ESG
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of internal company characteristics, namely profitability, company risk, and company size, on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance, as well as the moderating role of Good Corporate Governance (GCG). ESG has become an important indicator of corporate sustainability and long-term business performance, particularly in emerging markets where companies are increasingly expected to adopt sustainable and transparent business practices. This research employs a quantitative approach using secondary panel data from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2016–2023 period. The data were collected from annual reports, sustainability reports, and the Refinitiv database, and analyzed using panel data regression with a fixed effect model and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The findings indicate that profitability and company risk have a positive and significant effect on ESG performance, suggesting that companies with stronger financial capabilities and higher risk exposure tend to strengthen ESG implementation as part of their sustainability and risk management strategies. Meanwhile, company size does not significantly affect ESG performance, indicating that larger firms do not necessarily demonstrate better sustainability practices. The results also show that GCG significantly moderates the relationship between profitability and ESG as well as between company risk and ESG, but does not moderate the relationship between company size and ESG. These findings emphasize the importance of effective corporate governance in supporting sustainability strategies and improving ESG performance, particularly in the context of emerging markets such as Indonesia.

title: The Impact of Green Banking, Corporate Governance, and CSR on Financial Performance: Evidence from KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 Banks in Indonesia
summary: Financial performance reflects a bank's operational efficiency and systemic stability. Following regulatory shifts under POJK No. 12/POJK.03/2021, KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 banks face pressures to integrate sustainability and governance into their business models. This study investigates the impact of Green Banking, Corporate Governance, and Corporate Social Responsibility on banking financial performance. Using a quantitative causal approach, secondary data were gathered from annual and sustainability reports of KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2020 to 2024. The population comprised 16 banking firms, and a full sampling method yielded 80 observations. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model via EViews 14. The results demonstrate that Green Banking, measured by the Green Banking Disclosure Index, has a positive and significant effect on Return on Assets. Corporate Governance, proxied by Board Gender Diversity, shows no significant effect on financial performance. Conversely, Corporate Social Responsibility, measured by the CSR expenditure ratio, has a negative and significant effect on Return on Assets. These findings highlight that green disclosure enhances efficiency and stakeholder trust, whereas short-term CSR expenses act as direct operational costs

title: Decolonising Corporate Social Responsibility: A Bosadi-Informed Conceptual Framework for Social Sustainability and Restorative Justice in South African Mining Enclaves
summary: Contemporary Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks increasingly incorporate mitigating gender-based violence (GBV) as a core pillar of social sustainability. However, within emerging markets, particularly inside resource-rich sub-Saharan African extraction zones, these interventions systematically fail. They rely on Western-centric, neoliberal paradigms that prioritise corporate metric compliance over structural, community-level transformation. This conceptual paper introduces a novel theoretical synthesis that bridges decolonial criminology and sustainable development economics. By applying an African-centred Bosadi (womanhood) framework, this study overhauls corporate anti-GBV strategies, moving them away from top-down, state-centric formalistic policing toward localised, indigenous restorative justice systems. Grounded in a transparent, PRISMA-adapted systematic screening of 46 foundational peer-reviewed studies and institutional documents spanning 2015–2026, the paper presents a five-tiered synthesis of qualitative results and discussion. It exposes how multinational mining operations act as systemic criminogenic catalysts by driving extraction-induced land displacement, stripping rural women of agrarian livelihoods, and concentrating cash flow into male-dominated migrant networks. Furthermore, the paper critiques the performative nature of Eurocentric ESG metrics and demonstrates the institutional secondary victimisation inherent in formal policing. As an operational alternative, this study conceptualises the Bosadi-Informed Social Sustainability Framework, anchored by the Lekgotla la Bomme (The Women’s Council), localised grassroots safety hubs, and economic restitution networks. The framework demonstrates that decolonising victimology and restoring African women's financial autonomy are not merely ethical choices, but strict operational prerequisites for achieving genuine, long-term social sustainability and community economic resilience in the Global South.

title: COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES IN THE CORPORATE GOVERNANCE SYSTEM OF UKRAINIAN BANKING INSTITUTIONS
summary: Digital transformation of the banking sector is changing not only the technologies used to provide financial services but also corporate governance mechanisms, as the quality of managerial decisions increasingly depends on timely information, secure corporate communications, availability of analytical data, and banks’ digital operational resilience. The study aims to develop theoretical and methodological foundations for using communication and information technologies in the corporate governance of Ukrainian banking institutions and to construct a structural-functional model for their integration into governance processes. The object of the study is the information and communication support of corporate governance in banking institutions. The methodological framework combines systemic and structural-functional approaches with analysis and synthesis, comparison, systematisation, and content analysis of regulatory documents and international corporate and IT governance standards. The study substantiates the transition from considering digital technologies primarily as operational banking tools towards recognising them as an integral component of corporate governance. A three-level model of information and communication support is proposed, comprising communication, information-analytical, and control-security levels. Technologies are systematised across five functional areas: management decision support; corporate communication; risk management and internal control; disclosure and regulatory interaction; and digital operational resilience. Six criteria for assessing the effectiveness of information and communication support are identified: timeliness, completeness, reliability, traceability, security, and resilience of information flows. The proposed approach integrates IT governance into the overall corporate governance architecture and clarifies the responsibilities of the supervisory board, management board, risk management, compliance, internal audit, and IT functions. The practical significance of the findings lies in the possibility of applying the proposed model by supervisory and management boards of Ukrainian banks when developing digital governance policies, improving internal control systems, managing ICT-related risks, and increasing the quality and transparency of corporate decision-making.

title: Effects of Institutional Ownership, Independent Commissioners, and CSR Disclosure on ROA: the Moderating Role of Green Credit in Indonesian Conventional Banks
summary: Increasing commitment to sustainable finance has encouraged banks to strengthen corporate governance, improve the transparency of corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure, and expand environmentally responsible lending practices. Although previous studies have examined the associations of institutional ownership, independent commissioners, and CSR disclosure with financial performance, their findings remain mixed. Moreover, empirical evidence on the moderating role of green credit in these relationships remains limited, particularly among Indonesian conventional commercial banks. This study examines the associations of institutional ownership, independent commissioners, and CSR disclosure with bank financial performance and investigates the moderating role of green credit. Using a balanced panel dataset of 176 firm-year observations from 16 conventional commercial banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2014–2024, the study employs the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) to examine the direct associations and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) to assess the moderating role of green credit. The findings show that institutional ownership (β = 0.028, p = 0.022), independent commissioners (β = 0.019, p = 0.037), and CSR disclosure (β = 0.022, p = 0.033) are positively and significantly associated with return on assets (ROA). Green credit also significantly moderates the associations of institutional ownership (β = 0.047, p = 0.019), independent commissioners (β = 0.039, p = 0.027), and CSR disclosure (β = 0.062, p = 0.008) with ROA. The inclusion of green credit and its interaction terms increases the model's explanatory power from R² = 0.45 to R² = 0.61. These findings provide empirical evidence that governance mechanisms, CSR disclosure, and green credit are associated with bank financial performance and extend the application of Agency Theory and Stakeholder Theory within the sustainable finance context. The findings also offer practical considerations for regulators, policymakers, and bank managers regarding governance quality, CSR disclosure, and the development of green financing practices.

title: Is More Transparency Always Better? The Dilemma of AI-enabled ESG Disclosure in Supply Chains with Information Distortion
summary: This paper investigates how AI-enabled ESG management reshapes operational decisions in a supplier–retailer supply chain characterized by responsibility investment, information distortion, and consumer privacy concerns. We develop a game-theoretic model in which the supplier determines responsible input with a certain disclosure strategy, while the retailer decides whether to adopt AI for ESG reporting. The analysis shows that the supplier’s greenwashing or brownwashing behavior critically moderates the impact of AI adoption: when disclosure distortion is mild, AI enhances transparency, stimulates demand, and increases responsible input, whereas strong greenwashing weakens or even reverses these effects. The retailer’s AI adoption incentive depends on the interaction between disclosure distortion and penalty allocation, generating distinct adoption regions under different regulatory exposures. From the stakeholder perspective, consumer privacy sensitivity and information distortion jointly affect the impacts of AI on consumer surplus and social welfare. Overall, the results highlight the contingent value of AI-enabled ESG and offer managerial guidance on technology adoption, penalty design, and data-governance strategies in sustainable supply chain management.

title: ESG Performance, Corporate Governance, and Firm Value: The Mediating Role of Financial Sustainability new Emerging Markets in India
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and corporate governance have become increasingly important in corporate valuation, particularly in emerging markets where institutional conditions influence sustainability practices and financial outcomes. However, the mechanisms through which these factors are associated with firm value require further empirical investigation. This study aims to examine the relationships among ESG performance, corporate governance, financial sustainability, and firm value in Indian listed companies, with particular attention to the mediating role of financial sustainability. The research employed a quantitative approach based on 720 firm-year observations of non-financial listed firms in India. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, multicollinearity diagnostics, fixed-effects panel regression, and mediation analysis with bootstrapped confidence intervals were applied. Firm value was measured using Tobin's Q, while financial sustainability was assessed through the Sustainable Growth Rate. The results revealed positive associations between ESG performance, corporate governance, and firm value. ESG performance and corporate governance were also positively associated with financial sustainability, which demonstrated a significant relationship with firm value (β = 1.842, p < 0.01). The inclusion of financial sustainability increased the explanatory power of the firm-value model from 41.2% to 48.6%. Mediation analysis identified significant indirect effects of ESG performance (β = 0.0052) and corporate governance (β = 0.1551) on firm value through financial sustainability, with confidence intervals excluding zero. These findings indicate that financial sustainability partially mediates the examined relationships and represents an important financial mechanism associated with corporate valuation. The study contributes to emerging-market research by integrating ESG performance, corporate governance, and financial sustainability within a unified analytical framework. Further research should examine individual ESG dimensions, sectoral differences, alternative measures of financial sustainability, and potential endogeneity to establish the robustness of these relationships across different institutional environments.

title: Digital Transformation in Accounting and Business Administration: Current Practices and Future Direction
summary: Digital transformation is significantly reshaping accounting and business administration, driving substantial changes in efficiency, decision-making, and organizational dynamics. The integration of advanced technologies such as cloud computing, artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and data analytics is revolutionizing traditional accounting processes, making them more streamlined, accurate, and efficient. These innovations facilitate real-time data access, predictive analytics, and enhanced collaboration, allowing organizations to make more informed, data-driven decisions. However, the impact of digital transformation goes beyond technology, extending to organizational culture and workforce dynamics. Employees are required to adapt to new roles that focus on strategic decision-making, data interpretation, and innovation, necessitating continuous up-skilling and change management. While digital tools provide numerous benefits, they also bring challenges such as ethical concerns, cybersecurity risks, and workforce resistance to change. Ethical issues, including data privacy, bias in AI algorithms, and transparency, must be carefully addressed to maintain trust and regulatory compliance. Additionally, cybersecurity remains a critical concern as organizations increasingly rely on digital systems. To successfully navigate digital transformation, businesses must foster a culture of innovation, invest in employee training, and implement strong cybersecurity measures. By doing so, organizations can maximize the benefits of digital tools in Accounting and Business Administration, while addressing the challenges that come with them, ultimately ensuring long-term success and growth.

title: Digital Transformation in Accounting: A Qualitative Study of Independent Certified Public Accountants
summary: In recent years, the digital transformation experienced across professions has also brought a number of innovations to the accounting profession. In particular, the transfer of some accounting transactions to digital environments has made digital transformation in accounting more evident. Therefore, evaluating the views of accounting professionals regarding the digital transformation experienced in accounting is of importance. This study aims to determine the effects of digital transformation on accounting processes and Certified Public Accountants by revealing the views of independent Certified Public Accountants regarding the digital transformation experienced in accounting. Accordingly, the study examines the advantages and disadvantages of digital transformation, expectations from institutions and organizations, views on e-transformation applications, the adequacy of digital competence acquired through accounting education, and perceptions of digital transformation as an opportunity or threat. In this direction, a question form consisting of 6 questions regarding demographic characteristics and 5 semi-structured open-ended questions was created. Using this question form, interviews were conducted with 13 independent Certified Public Accountants registered with the Mardin-Şırnak Chamber of Certified Public Accountants. Descriptive analysis was used in the study, in which the qualitative research method was employed. The findings obtained were divided into main themes and subthemes in terms of content and meaning and interpreted. Accordingly, it was determined that the digital transformation experienced in accounting provides speed, time savings, and efficiency in accounting transactions and that independent Certified Public Accountants generally perceive digital transformation as an opportunity. In addition, it was concluded that accounting education remains inadequate in the face of the ongoing digital transformation and that problems are experienced regarding technical infrastructure and lack of training, risks associated with ensuring data security, and adaptation to digital transformation.

title: The Moderating Effect of Corporate Governance Quality on the Relationship Between Green Accounting Costs and Financial Performance: Evidence from Listed Manufacturing Companies in Nigeria
summary: This study examines the moderating role of corporate governance quality in the relationship between green accounting costs comprising safety-related costs, environmental protection costs, and pollution control costs and financial performance, measured by Economic Value Added (EVA), in 20 listed Nigerian manufacturing firms from 2014 to 2023 (200 firm-year observations). Using random effects panel regression with robust standard errors, results reveal that environmental protection and pollution control costs exert significant positive direct effects on EVA, while safety related costs show a positive but insignificant direct impact. Corporate governance quality significantly and positively moderates all three relationships, amplifying EVA gains most notably transforming the latent benefits of safety-related costs into measurable value. Anchored in stakeholder theory, these findings highlight governance as a critical enabler for sustainability driven performance in emerging markets, where institutional challenges persist. Implications for policy and practice emphasize integrated reporting and ESG-focused governance to unlock green investments' full potential.

title: From Research to Policy: Corporate Social Responsibility and Contemporary Challenges in Sustainable Development
summary: Abstract Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in India has come a long way from being a voluntary act of philanthropy to a mandated legal requirement. With the introduction of Section 135 in the Companies Act, 2013, India became the first country to legally mandate CSR spending. However, as we look at the present scenario, a pressing question arises: are we actually achieving sustainable development, or are companies just ticking boxes to comply with the law? This paper explores the journey of CSR from research to policy, highlighting the contemporary challenges like greenwashing, lack of standardised impact measurement, and the disconnect between corporate boardrooms and grassroots realities. Relying entirely on secondary data, including Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) reports and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) filings, this study evaluates how current CSR policies are faring. The findings suggest that while financial compliance has improved, the actual on-ground impact on sustainable development goals (SDGs) remains uneven. The paper concludes that for CSR to truly drive change, we need a shift from a 'spend-based' mindset to an 'impact-based' approach, backed by stricter policy frameworks and genuine stakeholder engagement.

title: Digital Internal Control: A Bibliometric Analysis
summary: Digital internal control has become a growing research domain as organizations integrate digital technologies into governance, risk management, and assurance processes. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis to map the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, collaboration patterns, and most influential works in digital internal control research. Data consisting of 66 documents published between 2002 and 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using VOSviewer through keyword co-occurrence, overlay, density, co-authorship, institutional, and country collaboration mapping, complemented by citation analysis. The results show that the field is organized around four thematic clusters: digital transformation and internal control effectiveness, internal control systems and information management in the digital economy, ESG performance and decision making, and a separate biomedical cluster in which the term internal control refers to laboratory quality assurance. The overlay visualization indicates a clear shift from engineering and laboratory applications toward corporate governance themes, with ESG performance, digitization, and internal control effectiveness emerging as the most recent topics. Citation analysis reveals that the most influential studies are empirical works from China linking digital transformation to internal control quality and firm productivity. Collaboration networks remain limited and fragmented, with China acting as the dominant hub, indicating substantial room for broader international and cross-institutional cooperation.

title: Managerial Discretion and Corporate Social Responsibility among Manufacturing Firms in Uganda: A Relative Importance Analysis
summary: Corporate social responsibility is key for firm sustainability since. The currenmt study seeks to establish the influence of managerial discretion on corporate social responsibility. Specific dimensions of managerial discretion that most powerfully drive Corporate social responsibility are not empirically tested. Prior studies treat managerial discretion as a composite, unidimensional construct, thereby obscuring which specific dimension of decision-making autonomy or internal organizational factors exerts the greatest influence on CSR. Using Relative Weights Analysis, this study examined the dimension-specific effects of managerial discretion on corporate social responsibility. A cross-sectional quantitative survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 314 medium and large manufacturing firms in Uganda using a structured self-administered questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analysis tested the dimension-specific hypotheses, and Relative Weights Analysis (RWA) was subsequently employed to determine the precise proportional contribution of each managerial discretion dimension to total CSR variance. Both dimensions of managerial discretion positively and significantly predicted CSR. Hierarchical regression results established decision-making autonomy as the stronger predictor (β = .583, p < .001) relative to internal organizational factors (β = .354, p < .001). RWA results corroborated and refined these findings: decision-making autonomy accounted for the larger proportion of explained CSR variance (RW = 58.2%, rescaled), while internal organizational factors contributed 41.8%. This study makes a dual methodological and substantive contribution. Methodologically, it is among the first studies in the managerial discretion-CSR literature to apply RWA. The study also generates dimension-specific empirical evidence from manufacturing firms in a developing-country African context where evidence on the differential importance of managerial discretion dimensions for CSR is not yet tested.

Sustainability Reporting has a negative and significant effect on Firm Value, while Good Corporate Governance, as proxied by institutional ownership, also does not have a significant effect on Firm Value. Simultaneously, Green Accounting, Sustainability Reporting, and Good Corporate Governance have a significant influence on Firm Value. title: Pengaruh Mekanisme Internal Corporate Governance terhadap Tingkat Leverage Keuangan pada Perusahaan Manufaktur yang Terdaftar di BEI Periode 2022-2024
summary: This study aims to test and analyze the influence of the internal corporate governance mechanism consisting of an independent board of commissioners, managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and audit committee on the level of financial leverage (Debt to Equity Ratio) in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022-2024 period. This study uses a quantitative approach with a sample of 57 companies selected through the purposive sampling method. The analysis technique used is panel data regression with a Random Effect Model (REM) model based on the results of the Chow Test, Hausman Test, and Langrange Multiplier Test. The results of the study show that simultaneously the four independent variables have a significant effect on leverage. However, partially, only institutional ownership has a negative and significant effect on leverage, while independent board of commissioners and managerial ownership have no significant effect on the negative direction, and the audit committee does not have a significant effect on the positive direction. These findings indicate that institutional investors have a more effective supervisory role than other internal governance mechanisms in controlling corporate debt policies.

title: Corporate Governance Variables and Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study examines the impact of corporate governance on the performance of manufacturing firms in Nigeria. Panel data were obtained from the audited annual reports of twenty (20) listed manufacturing firms covering the period 2020–2024. Corporate governance was proxied by board size and board diversity, while firm performance was measured using return on assets (ROA). The Panel Least Squares estimation technique was employed to analyze the relationship between the variables, following the confirmation of stationarity at levels using the Im, Pesaran, and Shin (IPS) and Levin, Lin, and Chu (LLC) unit root tests. The empirical results reveal that both board size and board diversity exert a negative and statistically significant effect on firm performance. These findings suggest that excessively large and highly independent boards may impede effective decision-making and reduce operational efficiency in Nigerian manufacturing firms. Based on the results, the study recommends that the selection and nomination of board members should be conducted through a transparent and rigorous process that emphasizes not only competence and qualifications but also an optimal balance in board composition to enhance firm performance.

title: The Mediating Role of Good Corporate Governance in the Relationship between ESG Performance and Financial Sustainability among MSMEs in Medan, Indonesia
summary: This study examines the relationship between ESG Performance and Financial Sustainability among Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) by investigating the mediating role of Good Corporate Governance (GCG). While previous studies have predominantly examined the direct effects of ESG practices on organizational performance in large corporations, evidence on how governance mechanisms transmit ESG effects to financial sustainability among MSMEs in developing economies remains limited. This study addresses this gap by testing an ESG–GCG–Financial Sustainability framework among MSMEs in Medan, Indonesia. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed using purposive sampling. Data were collected from 60 MSME owners and managers through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that ESG Performance has a positive and significant effect on GCG (β = 0.864, p < 0.001), while GCG positively and significantly affects Financial Sustainability (β = 0.953, p < 0.001). GCG also significantly mediates the relationship between ESG Performance and Financial Sustainability (β = 0.823, p < 0.001), indicating that governance mechanisms play an important role in translating ESG practices into sustainable financial outcomes. This study contributes empirical evidence from MSMEs in an emerging economy and highlights governance as a mechanism linking ESG practices with financial sustainability. The findings provide implications for MSME owners and policymakers seeking to strengthen sustainable business development through improved governance practices. The results should be interpreted cautiously due to the relatively small sample and single-city context.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Accounting Ethics, and Trust in Financial Reporting: Developing an Ethical AI Governance Framework
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally transforming accounting practice by displacing traditional data-processing tasks, augmenting auditing functions, and reshaping the professional competency requirements of financial reporting. While these technological developments generate substantial efficiency gains, they simultaneously introduce unprecedented ethical challenges, including algorithmic opacity, accountability diffusion, bias propagation in automated judgment, and the erosion of professional scepticism — that threaten the integrity of financial reporting and the public trust upon which the accounting profession's social licence to operate ultimately depends. This paper develops a rigorous, theoretically grounded analysis of the intersection between artificial intelligence and accounting ethics, drawing on institutional theory, agency theory, virtue ethics, and the stakeholder trust framework to diagnose how AI adoption reconfigures the ethical architecture of financial reporting and to prescribe the governance, professional, and regulatory responses required to safeguard ethical standards and trust in this transformed environment. The paper makes three original contributions: first, it develops a multi-dimensional taxonomy of AI-related ethical risks in accounting, distinguishing technical, professional, and systemic risk categories; second, it proposes the Ethical AI Accounting Governance Framework (EAAGF), an original implementation model that integrates algorithmic governance, professional ethics renewal, regulatory adaptation, and stakeholder assurance mechanisms; and third, it situates these contributions within a comparative empirical analysis of AI adoption experiences across major accounting contexts, integrating evidence from surveys, regulatory reports, and case illustrations. The paper argues that the central challenge is not whether AI will transform accounting — this is already occurring — but whether the profession, regulators, and organisations can collectively construct the ethical governance infrastructure required to ensure that transformation advances rather than undermines the accountability, transparency, and trust that constitute the profession's foundational social purpose.

title: From Finance to Impact: How Environmentally and Socially Responsible Investors Drive Integrated Reporting Globally
summary: ABSTRACT The interest of academics in Integrated Reporting (IR) has shifted over the years from identifying the determinants of its adoption to the factors that improve its quality. Among these, the ownership structure can play a fundamental role in its connection with companies' corporate governance and its influence on corporate disclosure. This study, through the analysis of 184 integrated reports, aims to increase the existing knowledge on the determinants of IR quality by analyzing its relationship with the presence of sustainable investors. Three types of investors are considered: the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) signatories, the investors with a long‐term perspective and the institutional investors. The results, interpreted in the light of the stakeholder theory and the institutional theory, demonstrate a positive effect of the presence of sustainable investors on the quality of the reports.
