title: Circular Supply Chains: Improving Inventory Decisions
summary: The circular economy has evolved from an aspirational slogan of ‘reduce-reuse-recycle’ to a driver of value. While supply chain managers and heads of sustainability initiatives have begun using techniques such as ‘closing the loop’ through recycling and ‘slowing the loop’ by extending product life, a key execution gap remains. Conventional supply chain moves in one direction: procure make sell. However, circular business models introduce complexity due to the reverse flow, the return journey of the products sold: sell use return/collect refurbish resell. This complexity stems from the uncertainty in the timing, quantity, and quality of returns, which overwhelms human decision-making. Recent Research by Sergey Naumov, Saurabh Bansal, and V. Daniel R. Guide reveals that even experienced managers succumb to ‘Supply Line Neglect’.1 If managers neglect the complexity of this reverse flow due to behavioural bias that causes them to overlook inventory already moving through reverse channels and over-order new stock to avoid perceived shortages, it could result in operating costs rising 300% to 700% above optimal benchmarks. The good news is that the research also uncovers strategies to mitigate this threat. For instance, decouple the uncertainty of the quality of returned products from the logistics planning. We unpack this strategy and other approaches to help de-risk a company’s sustainability logistics

title: Readiness and Acceptance of Accounting Information Systems for Financial Reporting in Indonesian Village-Owned Enterprises: A TRAM Approach
summary: Despite the growing adoption of digital accounting applications, there is limited evidence on how technology readiness influences the acceptance of accounting information systems within village-owned enterprises. This study examines the readiness and acceptance of accounting information systems used for financial reporting in Indonesian village-owned enterprises, using the Technology Readiness and Acceptance Model (TRAM). Data were collected through an online survey of personnel from village-owned enterprises involved in financial reporting and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that perceived usefulness is the strongest determinant of intention to use accounting information systems. Optimism positively influences perceived usefulness, while innovativeness positively affects perceived ease of use. Interestingly, insecurity also positively affects perceived usefulness, suggesting that concerns about data security, transaction reliability, and information accuracy may increase users’ appreciation of accounting applications. In contrast, perceived ease of use does not significantly influence intention to use. These findings indicate that technology adoption in village-owned enterprises is driven primarily by perceived practical benefits rather than operational simplicity. The study extends the application of TRAM to village-owned enterprises and suggests that technology readiness may operate differently in accountability-oriented rural organizations. Practically, adoption initiatives should emphasize the benefits of accounting applications for reporting quality, efficiency, and accountability.

title: Market capitalization as a stability challenge in the capital market: Evidence from Nepalese banking sector
summary: Traditional finance views stock market and portfolio choices as products, brand, market efficiency, investors' behavior, and rationality. However, research suggests that different factors affect the share market capitalization for its stability. The strategy's role of investment, innovation, SMEs, and financial sustainability has become more crucial for Nepalese economies driven by the interaction among the investors, financial markets, venture capital ecosystem, and sustainable finance. This exploratory study aims to examine the status of market capitalization and its financial determinants, explore the relationship between market capitalization and financial indicators, and analyze the impact of earnings per share (EPS), dividend payout ratio (DPR), return on equity (ROE), book value per share (BVPS), interest rates (IRs), and number of outstanding shares (NOSs) on market capitalization. The study employs a descriptive and causal-comparative research design, utilizing purposive sampling to select 10 commercial banks. The secondary data are acquired from the report of Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) and the annual report of the respective bank. The data is analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression analysis. The study's findings reveal a positive relationship between book value per share, outstanding shares, and market capitalization. In contrast, earnings per share, dividend payout ratio, return on equity, and interest rate do not significantly impact market capitalization. Thus, book value per share and outstanding shares are significant variables affecting market capitalization. The study concludes that structural financial indicators like book value per share and the number of shares are of greater importance in determining the market capitalization of Nepalese commercial banks than profitability and macroeconomic indicators. The study recommends that stakeholders in the Nepalese banking sector, including policymakers and management, adopt enhanced financial sustainability frameworks and regulatory support to foster sustainable growth and attract investors.

title: Problems of qualification of nazi propaganda in conditions of digital transformation
summary: Problem. In the context of digital transformation, extremist ideology, including Nazism, has acquired new forms of dissemination in information and telecommunication networks, which has significantly complicated the qualification of crimes related to Nazi propaganda. Aim. To identify and analyze the problems of qualification of crimes provided for in Articles 280, 282, 282.4 and 354.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, committed using information and telecommunication networks, and to propose criteria for their differentiation based on the dominant purpose of the act, as well as to formulate recommendations for improving law enforcement practice, taking into account modern forms of digital propaganda. Methods. The research material was based on the norms of the Russian criminal legislation (Articles 280, 282, 282.4, and 354.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation), resolutions of the Plenum of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, and case materials on Nazi propaganda in information and telecommunication networks for the period 2024–2025. The primary method employed was formal legal analysis, which allowed identifying common and distinguishing features of the elements of crimes. Results. Based on the analysis of Articles 280, 282, 282.4, and 354.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation and judicial practice materials for 2024–2025, the following issues were identified: problems of composition competition, determining the moment of crime commission in information and telecommunication networks, and distinguishing between public and private communication. The research proposed qualification criteria based on the dominant purpose of the act: rehabilitation of Nazi ideology (Article 354.1), inciting hostility using Nazi rhetoric as a tool (Article 282), and cumulative qualification in cases of two independent intentions. The study substantiated the need to expand the concept of Nazi propaganda to include modern digital forms such as meme culture, trolling, and automated systems. Conclusions. The current criminal legislation does not fully take into account the specifics of the digital environment, which generates legal conflicts in the qualification of Nazi propaganda in information and telecommunication networks. The key role in overcoming these conflicts belongs to the Plenum of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, which should provide clarifications on the issues of intent assessment and content orientation, as well as develop criteria for distinguishing public actions from private communication in the digital space.

title: TRANSFORMATION OF ELECTRONIC BUSINESS IN DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: One of the most significant changes that is happening today is the transition to an information society based on knowledge that intensively uses the Internet and other information and communication technologies in the execution of economic, business and daily life activities. The digital economy, as the main segment of this society, is characterized by the digitization of many products and services, as well as the use of the Internet and other networks in the execution of economic activities. Traditional markets are transforming into digital markets where fierce competition takes place in dynamic conditions, with rapid and major changes. This all led to changes in the way of conducting business, and especially in the way of managing business transactions with the company's trading partners. Electronic business and commerce (e-commerce) implies that every transaction takes place over the Internet and other networks, such as wireless mobile networks. E-commerce, on the other hand, enables the dynamic development of the digital economy. This work shows exactly how the transformation of e-business of companies takes place in the new circumstances dictated by the digital economy.

summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis proses pemberdayaan petani kopi melalui pemanfaatan program Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) di Desa Cibeusi, Kecamatan Ciater, Kabupaten Subang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kasus untuk memperoleh pemahaman yang mendalam mengenai proses pemberdayaan yang berlangsung pada kelompok tani penerima program CSR. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan studi dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan teknik analisis data interaktif melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan perspektif Green Social Work sebagai kerangka utama untuk memahami dimensi sosial dan ekologis, serta Creating Shared Value sebagai perspektif pendukung dalam menjelaskan penciptaan nilai bersama antara perusahaan dan masyarakat. Program tersebut juga mendorong meningkatnya partisipasi masyarakat, kesadaran ekologis, dan keberlanjutan usaha tani kopi. Dari perspektif Creating Shared Value, kemitraan antara perusahaan dan kelompok tani menghasilkan manfaat timbal balik berupa peningkatan kualitas produksi, keberlanjutan rantai pasok, dan penguatan hubungan sosial antara perusahaan dengan masyarakat. Penelitian ini menawarkan model pemberdayaan petani kopi berbasis CSR yang mengintegrasikan dimensi sosial, ekonomi, dan lingkungan sebagai kontribusi konseptual bagi pengembangan program pemberdayaan masyarakat berkelanjutan.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance dan Profitabilitas terhadap Dividend Payout Ratio pada Perusahaan LQ45 Periode 2023 - 2025
summary: This study was motivated by the uncertainty surrounding the factors influencing dividend policy in large Indonesian firms, particularly companies included in the LQ45 index. The study aimed to analyze the effect of institutional ownership, independent commissioners, audit committee size, and return on assets (ROA) on the dividend payout ratio (DPR) of LQ45 companies during the 2023–2025 period. A quantitative approach with an explanatory research design was employed, and the sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 25 companies and 75 observations. Secondary data were collected from annual reports and financial statements published by the Indonesia Stock Exchange, then analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results show that institutional ownership, independent commissioners, audit committee size, and return on assets (ROA) do not have a significant effect on the dividend payout ratio (DPR), either partially or simultaneously. These findings indicate that dividend policy in LQ45 companies during the study period was more likely influenced by other factors outside the variables examined, suggesting that future research should include additional variables such as financing structure, investment policy, and market conditions, as well as consider qualitative approaches for a more comprehensive understanding of dividend policy determinants.

title: TensorLock: Recovering Model Dependency for Model Supply Chain
summary: The public models on the model hosting platforms have undergone exponential growth, allowing developers to build upon existing models rather than training from scratch. These models are continuously reused, modified, and re-distributed similar to traditional software components, breeding a dense and rapidly evolving model supply chain. However, while enjoying the benefits of model reuse, developers also inherit supply chain risks ranging from legal liabilities to security threats. To mitigate these risks, a well-established model dependency graph can significantly benefit supply chain risk governance. Unfortunately, although model hosting platforms offer mechanisms for dependency disclosure, such declarations are optional and frequently missing. To address this challenge, we propose a novel model dependency recovering framework Tensorlock. It works in two phases; i.e., (1) model clustering, and (2) type-aware dependency identification within these clusters. In the first phase, Tensorlock performs connectivity-based clustering to accommodate the open-ended dependency topology, grouping models with dependency relations. In the second phase, Tensorlock employs a divide-and-conquer strategy, leveraging distinct type-specific fingerprints to first identify data-free dependencies (Quantization and Merging), and then resolve data-driven Fine-Tuning dependencies. Our evaluation demonstrates that Tensorlock substantially outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, achieving an ARI of 0.96 in clustering and a DF 1 of 0.82 in dependency identification, improving over the best baselines by at least 39% and 193%, respectively. Additionally, we apply Tensorlock to 289 supposedly isolated models and recover 189 previously missing model dependencies, with 42 model authors confirming our findings.

title: COMPARING ESG RATING APPLICATIONS IN THE CHINESE AND KAZAKHSTANI BANKING SECTORS
summary: The purpose of the research is to contrast ESG rating practices in Chinese and Kazakhstani banking industries, representing countries at different levels of ESG institutionalization. The methodology used in the research is a multi-method qualitative and descriptive study involving comparative approach, descriptive analysis, and case study methods. The Chinese sample consists of five largest banks operating in China – ICBC, CCB, ABC, CMB, and CITIC. They were evaluated according to Huazheng ESG index during 2020-2025. For Kazakh sample, there are five banks involved – Bank CenterCredit, Jusan Bank, Otbasy Bank, Development Bank of Kazakhstan, and Halyk Bank, which were evaluated according to the external ratings offered by S&P Global CSA, Sustainable Fitch, and MSCI/Sustainalytics. Overall, there are thirteen sources analyzed, out of which twelve represent peer-reviewed articles found within the Scopus database and academic journals of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The last source represents an official normative act of Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA). In general, China has created a full-fledged dual-system of ESG rating including domestic providers (Huazheng ESG), along with international agencies under strong regulations and regular data updating. On the other hand, the Kazakhstan banking industry is still at the beginning of its ESG evolution path. It is completely based on internationally recognized rating methodologies. There are no domestic rating systems in place; there is an immature regulatory system, and poor data availability, with the first ratings disclosed in 2022–2024 years, except for Halyk Bank that obtained its first MSCI rating in 2020. This work adds to the literature on comparative ESG studies by providing a well-developed institution-based bilateral analysis of a less studied country pair. title: Managing value of decommissioning obligations in mining industry – key challenging issues from the financial reporting perspective
summary: This article presents the evolution of financial reporting regulations and practices regarding decommissioning liabilities with a focus on the managerial approach to value creation processes in mining companies. Firstly, the author demonstrates the importance of provisions for the above-mentioned obligations for their overall financial standings. Than an analyses of the US and European financial reporting regulations from 1999 up to recent developments is provided to identify two fundamental challenges, related to: (a) a discount rate that should be applied to actualize cash flows needed to settle decommissioning liabilities, or broader, to proper inclusion of the risk factor into computations, (b) value recognition of post-retirement assets or broader, efficient management of these assets to maximize a mining project and company value. It has been proved that discounting is not a proper technique to deal with uncertainty of cash flows needed to settle decommissioning obligations, as mirroring a recognized practice applied for investment projects leads to results which are not only counterintuitive but significantly underestimate their current values. Therefore, a risk-free rate should be applied, and other methods must be developed to include uncertainty factors into computations. With respect to post-closure asset management, consequences of accounting treatment of gains from asset disposal have been analyzed. A need for adopting a broader perspective encompassing non-mining-related use of such assets in the ESG context was indicated. The article also demonstrates the value of mining industry experience for other industries facing similar problems, like renewable energy.

title: Development of Accounting Practices and Disclosure in the Light of the Shift towards Artificial Intelligence
summary: The purpose of this research is to contribute to the development of the accounting process and disclosure in the context of the disruption that brings in artificial intelligence by providing an integrated framework, from the perspective of internal development of accounting processes to the external requirements of the disclosure. The framework is based on the following five pillars: digital transformation policies; influence of artificial intelligence on the quality of accounting information; basic principles of intelligent models; governance mechanisms; and related risks. This is a descriptive and analytical study. It discussed the theoretical background and accounting implications of artificial intelligence, proposed a disclosure framework, and then it utilized content and gap analysis to determine to what extent the considered annual report met the requirements of the frameworkThe above analysis was based on the 2024 annual report of Asiacell Communications Company-Private Joint Stock Company. The disclosures of artificial intelligence, digital transformation, applications in accounting and finance, information quality, governance, and technological risk were selected and analyzed together with 24 disclosure items based on the proposed framework. The findings show a large disparity between the technological sophistication of the company and its level of accounting disclosure on artificial intelligence. The fermentations described in the present disclosure examples were at 25%, but only 25% of the disclosures were reached, and disclosures of assumptions underlying predictive models and related risks were missing. The results also suggest that the introduced framework, if adopted, would cover all the 24 disclosure items with a maximum proposed disclosure score of 100%.Also, based on model assumptions, data sources, levels of confidence, responsibilities in governance, and procedures for verification, transparency would be increased, the credibility of accounting estimates would be strengthened, the level of information uncertainty would be decreased, and the level of investor confidence in financial reports produced in an artificial intelligence milieu would be enhanced

title: Pengaruh Reputasi Audit, Audit complexity, Audit Tenure terhadap Audit delay
summary: This study examines the effects of audit reputation, audit complexity, and audit tenure on audit delay among Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. The population comprises all Consumer Non-Cyclicals companies consistently listed throughout the observation period. The sample was selected using purposive sampling based on companies that published complete audited financial statements, presented their financial statements in Indonesian rupiah, and provided the data required to measure all research variables. The final sample consists of 45 companies and 225 firm-year observations. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports, audited financial statements, and the official Indonesia Stock Exchange website. Audit delay is measured as the number of days between the fiscal year-end and the date of the independent auditor’s report. Audit reputation is measured using a dummy variable based on Big Four and non-Big Four affiliation. Audit complexity is proxied by the ratio of inventories and trade receivables to total assets, while audit tenure is measured by the number of consecutive years a company engages the same public accounting firm. The data are analyzed using panel data regression with the Fixed Effects Model and robust standard errors. The results show that audit reputation has a positive and significant effect on audit delay, audit complexity has no significant effect, and audit tenure has a negative and significant effect. This study contributes empirical evidence regarding the use of an account-based audit complexity proxy and the determinants of audit timeliness in the Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector. The study concludes that audit firm reputation and engagement duration affect audit completion time, whereas the proportion of inventories and trade receivables does not determine audit delay.

title: Audit Complexity dan Earning Quality: : Peran Sustainabilty Disclosure dan Audit Tenure
summary: This study examines the effect of Sustainability Disclosure and Audit Tenure on Earnings Quality, with Audit Complexity as a moderating variable. The study is motivated by the increasing demand for transparent financial reporting and the need to understand the conditions under which sustainability reporting and audit characteristics contribute to improving earnings quality. The research employs a quantitative approach using panel data from 26 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2021–2024 period, resulting in 104 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model selected as the most appropriate estimation model. The findings reveal that Sustainability Disclosure has a positive and significant effect on Earnings Quality, whereas Audit Tenure has no significant effect. Furthermore, Audit Complexity strengthens the positive relationship between Sustainability Disclosure and Earnings Quality, but weakens the relationship between Audit Tenure and Earnings Quality. These findings indicate that the effectiveness of sustainability disclosure in improving earnings quality depends on the level of audit complexity faced by the company. This study contributes to the development of Stakeholder Theory by demonstrating that Audit Complexity acts as a contingency factor influencing the effectiveness of corporate transparency and audit mechanisms in enhancing Earnings Quality. The findings also provide practical implications for management and auditors in improving the credibility of financial reporting, particularly in the energy sector.

title: Beyond Profit: Peran Corporate Social Responsibility and Business Ethics in Building Sustainable Business Performance through Strategic Planning pada UMKM
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Business Ethics on Sustainable Business Performance among culinary MSMEs producing traditional souvenirs in Jombang, East Java, with Strategic Planning as the mediating variable. The research was motivated by the tendency of culinary MSMEs to neglect social responsibility and business ethics due to the pressure of short-term profit orientation, as well as a research gap—few studies have examined the role of strategic planning as a mechanism that bridges CSR and business ethics with sustainable performance at the MSME level. The research design was quantitative-causal, employing purposive sampling of 106 SME operators under the guidance of the East Java Provincial Cooperative and SME Agency who employed at least one employee. Data were collected via a 1–5 Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The test results show that CSR and Business Ethics each have a significant positive effect on Sustainable Business Performance, both directly and through the mediation of Strategic Planning—which was found to be significant in both indirect pathways—while Strategic Planning was also found to have a significant positive direct effect on sustainable performance. This study makes a theoretical contribution to the literature on Stakeholder Theory and the Resource-Based View at the MSME level, as well as a practical contribution to the East Java Cooperative and MSME Office and culinary business operators in designing capacity-building programs that simultaneously integrate ethical, social, and strategic aspects.

title: Transformasi Digital dalam Akuntansi Keuangan: Systematic Literature Review Menggunakan Pendekatan PRISMA
summary: Aim: This study aims to analyze the development of digital transformation in financial accounting, identify dominant technologies and research themes, and explore research gaps in the field of digital transformation in financial accounting. Method: This study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. The data consist of scientific articles obtained from Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Emerald Insight, Google Scholar, and other scholarly sources. A total of 18 articles published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using content analysis with a thematic analysis approach. Results: The findings indicate that blockchain is the most dominant technology in the transformation of financial accounting due to its contribution to transparency, accountability, financial reporting quality, and fraud mitigation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation also play important roles in improving the efficiency of accounting and auditing processes and supporting data-driven decision-making. However, existing research remains largely dominated by conceptual and literature-based studies, while empirical research examining the implementation of digital technologies in accounting practices remains relatively limited. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: The novelty of this study lies in systematically mapping dominant technologies and research themes while identifying empirical research gaps. The findings imply that future research should integrate technology, governance, regulation, cybersecurity, and human resource competencies to support effective and sustainable digital transformation in financial accounting.

title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas, Likuiditas dan Audit Tenure terhadap Opini Audit Going Concern
summary: Transportation and logistics companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) provide services in the fields of transportation and supply chain management. To provide stakeholders with a clear picture of their internal condition for future decision-making, these business entities are required to publish audited financial statements. This study examines the influence of profitability, liquidity, and audit tenure on the issuance of going-concern audit opinions for companies in the transportation and logistics sector. A quantitative approach was employed, covering a population of 38 transportation and logistics companies over the 2021–2024 period. Using purposive sampling, 28 companies were selected for a four-year observation period, resulting in a final sample of 112 observations. The study relies on secondary data-specifically audited annual reports—obtained directly from the companies or the IDX. Data processing was conducted using logistic regression analysis via SPSS software (version 26). The findings indicate that profitability, liquidity, and audit tenure do not have a significant influence on going-concern audit opinions.

title: Управління прибутком у корпоративному обліку як проблема законності: концептуальна основа
summary: The relevance of this paper lies in the interplay between accounting policies and legal ethics, which remains at the forefront of contemporary discretionary accounting practices and the attendant earnings management. The paper's quest for understanding the legal consequences is relevant for corporate managers and investors, as it provides insight into the consequences of exceeding the boundaries of allowed accounting discretion, which brings regulatory oversight to the illegality of deceitful management of corporate earnings. Accordingly, the purpose of this paper is to analyse the legal repercussions of corporate engagement in earnings management. It also aims to investigate the causative factors of managerial engagement in earnings management and to develop a framework for the phenomenon. The methodological approach focused on critical reviews and the application of doctrinal and comparative research methods to analyze related documents, including those from regulatory bodies, associated cases, and published journal articles, employing a thematic framework. The results show, on the one hand, that earnings management beyond policy limits may result in financial fraud and/or filing deceits, and that such actions could attract various legal enforcement consequences, including fines, penalties, job loss, company closures, and imprisonment, among others. On the other hand, the results also indicate that corporate management may be lured into illegal earnings management primarily to promote the company's financial outlook and to serve management's economic interests. The paper presents some promising avenues for further research. Such a future could explore the different levels of legal consequences when management exploits accounting policy loopholes, mainly to deceive investors into believing that the company is financially buoyant, versus the legal repercussions when such exploitation is primarily for management's self-financial gain, such as in earnings management and tunneling engagements. A comparison of regional differences in earnings management and differences in legal consequences could offer investors insights into which regions have more substantial legal repercussions and, therefore, stronger deterrents for managers to engage in earnings management

title: ESG and Financial Risk: Does AI Innovation Strengthen the Relationship?
summary: This study aims to examine the impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on a firm’s financial risk and to explore the moderating role of Artificial intelligence (AI) innovation. This research uses a quantitative approach with secondary data from Indonesia companies listed on Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2018 – 2024, resulting in 340 observations. The firm financial risk is measured using Altman Z-Score and Zmijewski X-Score, while the analysis is conducted using panel regression with fixed effects. The results show that ESG performance does not have a significant effect on financial stability as measured by Z-Score, suggesting that the financial benefits of implementing ESG might not be immediately visible in the short-term. However, ESG significantly reduces financial distress risk as measured by the X-Score, indicating that stronger ESG practices increase financial resilience. AI innovation contributes to improving financial outcomes, but does not consistently strengthen them. Overall, this study concludes that ESG performance supported by AI innovation has the potential to lower financial distress. This study contributes to the growing sustainability finance literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging market on how ESG performance and AI innovation jointly influence firm financial risk.

title: Geopolitical disruptions and Saudi Arabia’s emergence as a global logistics stabilisation hub
summary: Background: Global supply chains remain highly exposed to geopolitical instability affecting critical maritime chokepoints across the Middle East, including the Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal. Disruptions in these corridors can reverberate through logistics networks, increase supply chain risk exposure and weaken trade continuity. Objectives: This study examines whether Saudi Arabia can function as a logistics stabilisation hub by connecting Red Sea gateways, Gulf ports, inland logistics corridors, energy logistics assets and digital logistics systems. Method: A structured survey of 300 logistics professionals was analysed using structural equation modelling. The model tested the relationships between geopolitical instability, maritime logistics disruptions, supply chain risk exposure, logistics stabilisation hub capability and supply chain stability. Results: Geopolitical instability increased maritime logistics disruptions, and maritime disruptions increased supply chain risk exposure. Supply chain risk exposure reduced global supply chain stability. Logistics stabilisation hub capability moderated the disruption–stability relationship and supported regional supply chain resilience. Conclusion: National logistics systems can reduce the destabilising effects of maritime chokepoint disruption when they provide multimodal redundancy, energy-logistics continuity and digital cargo visibility. Contribution: The study extends hub theory by framing logistics hubs as stabilisation infrastructure rather than only trade facilitation assets.

title: Supply Chain Network-Based Path Optimization for Customized Product
summary: The increasing demand for customized products has significantly increased the complexity of supply chain operations, making efficient path planning an important issue for reducing overall supply chain costs. This study proposes a supply chain network (SCN)-based path optimization model for customized product supply chains. The proposed model simultaneously optimizes node selection and transportation routes while minimizing transportation, processing, and fixed operating costs. To solve the optimization problem, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) with integer encoding is employed. Numerical experiments are conducted under different supply chain network scales to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The experimental results indicate that the proposed approach can effectively identify cost-efficient node configurations and transportation routes while maintaining stable convergence across different network scales. The proposed model provides an effective optimization framework for customized product supply chain design and offers useful managerial implications for supply chain network planning and cost management.

title: Digital transformation of professional training in the prison system
summary: The article examines the strategic priorities of state policy and the main technological trends in the digitalization of vocational education in the penitentiary system of the Russian Federation. Systemic problems related to the readiness of the teaching staff to work in the digital environment are identified, and a gap between the teacher’s self‑assessment and their actual level of proficiency with digital tools is recorded. The results of empirical studies confirm a high adaptive potential but highlight the need for specialized secure platforms under the conditions of regime restrictions. The necessity of developing departmental advanced training programs, a motivation system, and a shift towards qualitative performance indicators is substantiated. Measures are proposed to establish ethical and legal norms for the use of AI, aimed at balancing technological sovereignty with the preservation of the fundamental nature of staff training.

title: The Implementation of Smart Farming and Integrated Supply Chains to Ensure Food Security and Price Stability in East Java
summary: Objective: This study aims to analyze the implementation of Smart Farming and supply chain integration as strategies to ensure food security and price stability in East Java. Design/Methods/Approach: This study used a descriptive qualitative document-analysis design. The study purposively selected government policy documents, official publications, program reports, and peer-reviewed articles, then analyzed them using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis—coding combined deductive categories derived from the research objectives with inductive codes emerging from the documents. Source triangulation, a document-extraction matrix, an audit trail, and repeated theme review strengthened analytical trustworthiness. Findings: The research findings indicate that the implementation of Smart Farming, including soil moisture monitoring, crop growth sensors, and data-driven weather forecasting, contributes to increased productivity and reduced crop losses. Supply chain integration through digital platforms and cooperative collaboration has also been shown to support more efficient distribution and help mitigate price fluctuations. Originality/Value: This study provides insights into how Smart Farming technology and supply chain integration can contribute to food security and price stability in East Java, addressing both agricultural efficiency and market stability. Practical/Policy implication: This study recommends strengthening technology adoption, policy support, and supply chain partnerships as strategic steps towards sustainable food security in East Java.

title: Sustainability and reverse supply chain, the mediating role of ecological innovation
summary: The mounting obstacles of waste management and the increasing importance of ecological innovation, reverse supply chains become apparent tactic by organizations for resource retrieval, value creation, and reducing environmental footprint .This study examines the influence of sustainable practices such as sustainable procurement, green supplier collaboration, management commitment and environmental regulations on reverse supply chain with the mediation of ecological innovation in Iraqi small and medium enterprises. The study adopted a quantitative design and the data were collected from 350 questionnaire survey sent to owners and managers of manufacturing firms in Iraq. The author employed (PLS-SEM) to analyze the relationship among variables. The results show sustainable procurement, green supplier collaboration, top management commitment positively impacted ecological innovation. In contrast, environmental regulations have no direct effect on ecological innovation. This outcome can be explained by weak enforcement of environmental regulations in Iraq. In addition, ecological innovation mediates the relation between procurement, green supplier collaboration, top management commitment and reverse supply chain. This study exposes how ecological innovation acts as the internal bridge that transforms general sustainability practices into concrete, efficient reverse supply chain operations, addressing a key gap in manufacturing and logistics research.

title: EXTERNAL ASSURANCE QUALITY AND THE VALUATION OF SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE
summary: This research investigates the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on firm value by considering the quality of external assurance in the Indonesian capital market. Using a quantitative approach, the study analyzes 87 firm-year observations of publicly listed companies with available ESG data and sustainability reports during 2022–2024. The hypotheses are tested using panel data regression and moderated regression analysis. The robustness tests are also performed using alternative proxies for firm value. The results reveal that ESG performance significantly enhances a company’s market valuation. Furthermore, the quality of external assurance fails to moderate the positive effect of ESG performance on a firm's market valuation. This study extends the existing literature by examining the quality of external assurance as a moderating variable in the relationship between ESG performance and firm value in the Indonesian capital market, where empirical evidence remains limited. This research enriches the current literature by providing empirical evidence that ESG performance functions as a critical signaling mechanism for investors when assessing a company's prospects and sustainability. The findings encourage companies to improve ESG performance, regulators to standardize external assurance, and investors to incorporate ESG into investment decisions.

title: Absolute Sustainability by Design: From Molecules to Processes, Supply Chains, and Planetary Boundaries
summary: Chemists want to design molecules and catalysts that are environmentally sustainable. But whether a new molecule is sustainable does not depend on its structure and reaction alone. It depends on the system built around it: the reactor and separation steps used at scale, the utilities supplying them such as electricity and high-temperature heat, the supply chains delivering feedstocks and products, and how all of this fits into a pathway towards a future net-zero circular economy that stays within the safe operating space of the planet. We present the vision of an integrated toolchain that spans these scales, from molecular design to planetary boundaries. The toolchain combines four pillars: (i) computer-aided molecular and process design [1] to identify promising candidate molecules and their most efficient industrial synthesis routes, (ii) time-explicit life cycle assessment [2] to evaluate environmental impacts dynamically by accounting for evolving future production systems, (iii) transition pathway optimization [3] for strategic deployment planning and the design of robust, long-term supply chain networks, and (iv) absolute sustainability assessment [4], which evaluates system-wide environmental impacts against the planetary boundary framework to ensure future pathways do not transgress ecological limits. By equipping chemists with an accessible yet comprehensive framework, this toolchain bridges the gap between molecular design and systems engineering. Researchers can anticipate the macro-level consequences of micro-level design choices early in development, avoiding regrettable substitutions where a molecule appears sustainable in the lab but creates severe environmental bottlenecks at industrial scale. title: The Regulatory Architecture of Sustainable Development: Corporate Accountability, Legal Compliance, and the Governance of ESG Integration
summary: The governance of sustainable development has undergone a profound legal transformation as regulatory frameworks increasingly mandate corporate accountability for environmental, social, and governance performance. This article examines the evolving legal architecture governing sustainable development management, with particular focus on the European Union's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, and their extraterritorial implications for global business governance. Drawing upon regulatory theory, corporate governance scholarship, and comparative legal analysis, the article argues that the convergence of sustainability management with legal compliance obligations represents a paradigmatic shift in how corporations internalise sustainable development objectives. The analysis reveals that while regulatory frameworks have created unprecedented transparency and accountability mechanisms, significant challenges persist regarding enforcement consistency, jurisdictional fragmentation, and the balance between regulatory ambition and business competitiveness. The article proposes a governance model grounded in regulatory coherence, proportionate liability, and transnational regulatory convergence to harmonise sustainable development imperatives with corporate operational realities. The findings carry implications for corporate managers, compliance officers, policymakers, and scholars seeking to navigate the intersection of law and sustainable development governance.

title: AI-Based Inventory Management and Operational Efficiency
summary: Abstract The increasing complexity and dynamism of global supply chains have rendered traditional inventory management approaches insufficient for meeting contemporary operational demands. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative capabilities for inventory optimization through enhanced demand forecasting, automated replenishment, cost reduction, and supply chain resilience. This paper examines the integration of AI technologies in inventory management and their impact on operational efficiency through a systematic literature review and analysis of real-world case studies. The findings reveal that machine learning and deep learning models substantially outperform traditional statistical methods in demand prediction accuracy, particularly for intermittent and volatile demand patterns. AI-driven automated replenishment systems reduce stockouts and excess inventory, while predictive analytics enable proactive risk mitigation. Case analyses of Amazon, Walmart, and Zara demonstrate that organizations leveraging AI achieve measurable improvements in inventory turnover, waste reduction, and supply chain responsiveness. The paper concludes with a discussion of implementation challenges and future research directions, including the potential of generative AI and digital twin technologies.

title: FROM LEDGERS TO ALGORITHMS: MAPPING FINTECH'S IMPACT ON FINANCE AND ACCOUNTING THROUGH BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS (1989–2025)
summary: This study examines the impact of financial technologies (FinTech), management information systems, and artificial intelligence (AI) on finance, accounting, and business processes. It explores how AI-supported FinTech applications contribute to risk management, security, customer experience, and transaction automation, while discussing their advantages and limitations. Publications indexed in the Web of Science database between 1989 and 2025 were analyzed. A total of 3,691 documents were examined using bibliometric analysis to identify publication trends, collaboration structures, and key conceptual themes. The findings reveal significant growth in FinTech research, with AI emerging as a central research theme. China and the United States lead AI integration in FinTech research. Major challenges include data privacy, cybersecurity, and algorithmic bias. Although AI improves financial services, risk management, and business processes, it cannot fully replace human judgment. The study identifies research gaps and future directions for integrating FinTech, AI, accounting information systems, and business processes.

title: Effect of Digital Transformation on Smart Business Model Adoption in Retail Firms: Evidence from fsQCA
summary: As smart business model innovation has become a strategic priority for retail companies looking to improve their competitiveness, digital transformation has emerged as a strategic imperative. But the research to date generally only considers the individual impacts of digital transformation capabilities, with linear analytical approaches, offering limited knowledge about the interactions of capabilities in the adoption of smart business models. This study aims to fill this gap by exploring the configurational pathway to the adoption of smart business models within retail companies in China. The study is based on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) Framework that considers the roles of digital leadership, digital technology capability, organizational agility, digital skills, and customer digital orientation. A structured questionnaire with five-point Likert-scale measures was used to collect data from 130 managers from Chinese retail companies. The data were analysed using Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), which was used to draw out the necessary and sufficient conditions and configurations for high smart business model adoption. The findings show that the necessary condition for smart business model adoption is capability with digital technology. In addition, three other types of digital transformation capabilities are found, showing that smart business models can be adopted on multiple strategic paths within retail. The findings also validate the concepts of equifinality and causal asymmetry which means that the configurations that contribute to successful adoption of a business model are different from those that contribute to unsuccessful adoption. It makes a contribution to the literature on digital transformation and business model innovation by using a configurational approach to capability integration and it expands the use of fsQCA in the research on digital transformation. The results also provide valuable recommendations for retail managers and policy makers looking to push digital transformation faster and to create smart and sustainable business models in an ever-competitive digital economy.

title: Systematic bias in Scope 3 emissions accounting: evidence from firm-level supply networks
summary: Scope 3 emissions often constitute the largest share of corporate greenhouse gas footprints, yet their accounting remains highly sensitive to incomplete supplier-level information and the replacement of aggregated emission-intensity proxies. Here, using Toyota Motor Corporation as a firm-level case study, we examine the data gap of third-party supply-chain databases and assess how the granularity and source of emission-intensity data shape upstream Scope 3 estimates. We construct a five-tier supply-chain network for this company, drawing upon publicly available supplier-customer relationships, firm financial reports, geographic information and a gravity model used for trade volumes prediction, which is therefore conservative, transparent, and reproducible for shareholders to implement and verify. Benchmark with the network constant, four emission-intensity scenarios, ranging from firm-level intensities to subindustry-, sector-, and MRIO-based sector averages are compared. Results show that sector-average emission intensities would overestimate the Scope 3 emissions; the magnitude of the overestimates hinges on the data scales and database selections. This study further reveals a pronounced emissions concentration, with the first-tier suppliers accounting for around 60% of upstream embodied emissions across the five supply tiers. A similar emissions concentration also exists among a small number of carbon-intensive suppliers within each supply tier; most of them are engaged in raw materials provision and energy-intensive activities. Firm-level analysis of emission hotspots also demonstrates that trade network reconstruction can improve the interpretability and decision relevance of corporate Scope 3 accounting by revealing where embodied emissions are concentrated and how mitigation efforts can be prioritized across global supply networks.

title: Pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan Leverage terhadap Kinerja Keuangan Perusahaan pada PT Astra International Tbk Periode 2016-2025
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan leverage terhadap kinerja keuangan PT. Astra International Tbk periode 2016-2025, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan dan laporan tahunan perusahaan selama periode penelitian, yang dianalisis menggunakan uji t untuk melihat pengaruh parsial dan uji F untuk melihat pengaruh simultan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial CSR berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan (signifikansi 0,037 < 0,05; t-hitung 2,670 > t-tabel 2,364), sedangkan leverage tidak berpengaruh signifikan (signifikansi 0,086 > 0,05; t-hitung 2,050 < t-tabel 2,364). Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa pengungkapan CSR lebih dominan dalam memengaruhi persepsi kinerja keuangan dibandingkan tingkat leverage perusahaan. Implikasinya, perusahaan disarankan untuk terus meningkatkan kualitas dan konsistensi pengungkapan CSR sebagai strategi peningkatan kinerja keuangan, sementara kebijakan leverage perlu dikelola secara hati-hati meski pengaruhnya belum signifikan secara statistik dalam penelitian ini.

title: The Effect of Sales Growth, Asset Efficiency, and Capital Structure on Financial Performance with Corporate Social Responsibility as a Moderating Variable: A Study on Consumer Non-Cyclical Companies
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of sales growth, asset efficiency, and capital structure on financial performance, with corporate social responsibility (CSR) as a moderating variable in consumer non-cyclical companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. The research population comprised all 131 companies in the consumer non-cyclical sector listed on the IDX. Through purposive sampling, a final sample of 15 companies was obtained, yielding 75 observations over the five-year period. Secondary data from annual financial and sustainability reports were collected using the documentation technique. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) approach. The t-test results indicate that sales growth and asset efficiency have a significant positive effect on financial performance, while capital structure has a significant negative effect. Furthermore, the moderation analysis reveals that CSR disclosure significantly strengthens the positive impact of sales growth on financial performance but weakens the positive impact of asset efficiency on financial performance. However, CSR is unable to moderate the effect of capital structure on financial performance. The implications of this study emphasize that integrating CSR practices can serve as a strategic catalyst to optimize sales growth for sustainable financial performance.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE ENTERPRISE ECONOMIC SECURITY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM IN THE CONTEXT OF EUROPEAN INTEGRATION AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
summary: The article examines the theoretical and applied aspects of the digital transformation of the enterprise economic security management system in the context of European integration and the implementation of sustainable development principles. It is substantiated that digitalization is transforming enterprise management approaches by reshaping economic security mechanisms, business process organization, and managerial decision-making systems. The study establishes that the adoption of advanced digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, big data, cloud computing, the Internet of Things, robotic process automation, and digital platforms, creates new opportunities to enhance management efficiency while simultaneously generating new risks and threats. The impact of digital transformation on the activities of Ukrainian enterprises is analyzed. The findings demonstrate that digitalization improves business process transparency, enhances management efficiency, strengthens predictive analytics, and increases the competitiveness of enterprises within the European economic area. At the same time, digital transformation intensifies cybersecurity, information, organizational, human resource, legal, and financial risks, highlighting the need to improve enterprise economic security management systems. The study systematizes the key challenges associated with digital transformation and proposes an author's approach to identifying the priority directions for the digital transformation of enterprise economic security management systems. These include the digitalization of management processes, the implementation of intelligent decision support systems, business process automation, cybersecurity enhancement, digital asset management, cloud technology adoption, logistics digitalization, and the integration of ESG principles into economic security management. The scientific novelty of the research lies in the development of a comprehensive model for the digital transformation of the enterprise economic security management system. The proposed model integrates environmental factors, strategic objectives, digital transformation components, economic security management processes, resource support, transformation outcomes, and a continuous improvement mechanism. The practical significance of the research lies in the applicability of the proposed approaches to developing digital transformation strategies, improving corporate digital development policies, strengthening risk management, and facilitating enterprise adaptation to the requirements of the European economic environment.

title: The Interplay of Carbon Policy and Social Dynamics in Supply Chain Decarbonization: A Network Systems Approach
summary: Decarbonizing supply chains is a complex systemic challenge where institutional constraints such as carbon policies intersect with behavioral responses including social dynamics within intricate network structures. Existing studies often examine these factors in isolation, overlooking their coupled systemic interactions. This paper adopts a network systems approach to investigate how carbon quota constraints and conformity behavior jointly shape the evolution of low-carbon transitions within supply chain industrial clusters. Using a Watts–Strogatz small-world network as the structural carrier, we develop an evolutionary system model that integrates individual economic rationality with social learning dynamics. By combining analytical derivations with Monte Carlo simulations, we reveal the critical systemic thresholds arising from this interplay. The results indicate that while carbon policy sets the economic baseline, its effectiveness is profoundly modulated by social dynamics. Specifically, conformity exhibits a critical threshold effect: moderate conformity slows diffusion but ultimately allows economic incentives to prevail; however, extreme conformity overwhelms economic signals, leading to a systemic high-carbon lock-in. Furthermore, network topology acts as a crucial regulator: small-world structures with moderate rewiring optimally balance local coordination and global spread, effectively buffering the negative impacts of conformity. Carbon pricing demonstrates a strict economic threshold, above which the system undergoes a phase transition towards full decarbonization, though with diminishing marginal returns. Finally, core nodes can act as breakthrough agents under moderate conformity but lose their advantage under extreme social pressure. These findings provide a systems-level understanding of supply chain decarbonization, offering actionable insights for designing carbon policies that account for behavioral dynamics and optimizing industrial network structures to foster sustainable transitions.

title: Impact of Digitalization on Supply Chain Efficiency at Ram Transporters Limited, Rwanda
summary: Abstract: This study examined the relationship between digitalization and supply chain efficiency at RAM Transporters Ltd in Rwanda. It focused on three dimensions of digitalization: real-time data monitoring, automated order processing and scheduling, and digital procurement systems. A descriptive cross-sectional research design employing a mixed-methods approach was adopted. The target population comprised 45 employees of RAM Transporters Ltd. Quantitative data were collected using questionnaires, of which 35 complete responses were obtained, while qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with five key informants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson’s correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression in SPSS Version 25, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The findings indicated a low overall level of digitalization, with a digitalization index of 34.4%. Real-time monitoring recorded the highest mean score (M = 2.45), followed by automated scheduling (M = 1.95) and digital procurement (M = 1.65), while supply chain efficiency had an overall mean score of 2.10. Pearson’s correlation analysis revealed positive and statistically significant relationships between real-time monitoring and supply chain efficiency (r = .645, p < .01) and between automated scheduling and supply chain efficiency (r = .521, p < .01). The multiple regression model explained 48.7% of the variance in supply chain efficiency, with real-time monitoring emerging as the only statistically significant individual predictor (β = .432, p = .024). Qualitative findings further revealed continued reliance on manual processes, fragmented use of digital technologies, and resistance to technological change. The study concludes that digitalization is significantly associated with supply chain efficiency at RAM Transporters Ltd, with real-time monitoring showing the strongest measurable relationship in the regression model. The study recommends strengthening real-time monitoring systems, progressively automating core supply chain processes, developing integrated digital procurement systems, and investing in staff training and change-management initiatives. title: Pengaruh Pergantian Auditor, Kepemilikan Institusional, dan Audit Fee terhadap Audit Delay
summary: Timely audited financial reporting is important for investors and other stakeholders, yet audit delay remains a concern among listed companies, including those in the property and real estate sector. This study examines the effect of auditor switching, institutional ownership, and audit fee on audit delay in property and real estate companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2019–2024. The study employed a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports and financial statements. Using purposive sampling, 33 companies were selected, resulting in 198 firm-year observations. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with EViews 12. The findings indicate that auditor switching and audit fee significantly affect audit delay, while institutional ownership does not have a significant effect. Simultaneously, auditor switching, institutional ownership, and audit fee significantly affect audit delay. These findings indicate that changes in auditors and audit fee are relevant factors in understanding variations in audit completion time, whereas institutional ownership alone does not appear sufficient to determine audit delay in the observed companies.

title: A strategic framework for supply chain optimization in pharmaceutical SMEs: an empirical study
summary: Purpose This study investigates the supply chain challenges faced by pharmaceutical SMEs in India. It aims to identify critical operational gaps and develop an empirically validated framework to improve efficiency, regulatory compliance and overall competitiveness. Design/methodology/approach A mixed methods approach was adopted, combining a comprehensive literature review, expert interviews and survey data from 96 Indian pharmaceutical SMEs. The qualitative phase explored issues in procurement, technological integration and logistics. Quantitative validation was performed using Exploratory Factor Analysis and cluster analysis, which distilled the challenges into five dimensions: innovation and traceability, strategic risk management, warehouse and inventory management, compliance and collaboration and customer relationship management. Findings The analysis reveals significant disparities in supply chain practices, categorizing SMEs into three clusters: Strategic Growth Leaders, Struggling Sustainers and Future Driven Innovators. Key challenges include stringent regulatory compliance, limited financial resources and inadequate technological adoption. The proposed framework offers targeted strategies to address these gaps, demonstrating potential for improved operational performance and financial outcomes. Originality/value This research provides a novel, integrated framework linking supply chain performance with financial metrics in the context of pharmaceutical SMEs. By offering actionable insights for both practitioners and policymakers, the study contributes uniquely to the literature on SME supply chain management in emerging economies.

title: Aflatoxin Contamination in the Maize Supply Chain: A Case of Nampula Province, Mozambique
summary: Aflatoxin contamination in maize remains a major food safety and public health concern in Nampula Province, Mozambique. Maize samples obtained from farmers, traders, and milling units across the districts of Malema, Mossuril, Mecuburi, Monapo, and Nampula in 2024 and 2025 were analysed using UPLC-ESI-MS/MS. In 2024, aflatoxins were detected in samples from Mecuburi (43%), Mossuril (17%), Monapo (17%), and traders (13%), with some exceeding the regulatory limit of 15 µg/kg. AFB1 was the predominant aflatoxin, followed by AFB2. At the farmer level, Mecuburi recorded the highest contamination, with AFB1 and AFB2 detected in 43% of samples and AFG1 and AFG2 in 29%, while Mossuril had 20% contamination with AFB1 and AFG1. The maximum concentration was 4221.33 µg/kg of AFB1 in Mecuburi, whereas the minimum detected concentration was 2.82 µg/kg of AFB2. Aflatoxins were not detected above the limit of detection in milling samples or in samples collected in 2025. Despite the relatively low prevalence, the occurrence of extremely high aflatoxin concentrations highlights persistent contamination risks and the need for integrated mitigation strategies throughout the maize supply chain.

title: Digital Transformation and Economic Growth: A Case Study of India
summary: The relationship between Digital Transformation (DT) and economic growth is a subject of intense debate. Defined broadly, DT means the development (or integration) of digital technologies with other economic activities, intended to improve productivity, efficiency and governance. In the last decade, Indian economy witnessed a paradigm shift in the development and diffusion of DT, driven by a series of policy initiatives viz. Aadhar, DigiLocker and BharatNet. Further, at a macro level, emergence and convergence of new technologies in the form of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Blockchains, cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT) etc., are not only reshaping the industrial structure but also creating new business models of production, information, consumer preferences or the delivery system (like online payment, e-commerce and E-Governance). The very foundation of 4IR (4th Industrial Revolution) rests on the DT directly and indirectly. Given the unprecedented growth and development of DT, the paper attempts to understand the theoretical relationship between DT and economic growth by identifying various channels and mechanisms through which the relationship works. The theory is further corroborated by empirical evidence from advanced countries across different time periods. Given this, the study delves deeper into drawing inferences about the relationship in case of the Indian economy, the fastest emerging economies in the world. The time period considered is since 1991, i.e. the period of economic reforms leading to the emergence of DT.

title: Pengaruh Green Accounting, Kinerja Keuangan dan Good Corporate Governance terhadap Penghindaran Pajak pada Perusahaan Manufaktur di Bursa Efek Indonesia Tahun 2021-2024
summary: Penelitian ini mengkaji hubungan antara akuntansi hijau, kinerja keuangan, dan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik serta pengaruhnya terhadap penghindaran pajak di antara perusahaan manufaktur yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (IDX) selama periode 2021–2024. Isu penghindaran pajak penting karena keputusan pajak perusahaan dapat dikaitkan dengan kondisi keuangan, praktik akuntansi lingkungan, dan implementasi tata kelola perusahaan. Penelitian ini mengadopsi pendekatan kuantitatif menggunakan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan perusahaan, laporan tahunan, dan laporan keberlanjutan yang dipublikasikan selama periode pengamatan. Data dikumpulkan dari situs web resmi Bursa Efek Indonesia dan pengungkapan perusahaan yang relevan. Sampel ditentukan melalui purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditentukan, menghasilkan 21 perusahaan manufaktur dan total 84 observasi. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) versi 25. Prosedur analitis terdiri dari analisis statistik deskriptif, uji asumsi klasik, dan analisis regresi linier berganda. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa akuntansi hijau memiliki pengaruh positif dan signifikan secara statistik terhadap penghindaran pajak. Sebaliknya, kinerja keuangan memiliki pengaruh negatif dan signifikan secara statistik terhadap penghindaran pajak. Sementara itu, tata kelola perusahaan yang baik tidak memiliki pengaruh yang signifikan secara statistik terhadap penghindaran pajak. Koefisien determinasi menunjukkan nilai Adjusted R Square sebesar 0,364, yang mengindikasikan bahwa akuntansi hijau, kinerja keuangan, dan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik secara kolektif menjelaskan 36,4% variasi dalam penghindaran pajak. Sisanya, 63,6%, disebabkan oleh faktor-faktor lain di luar model penelitian.

title: Blockchain Based Solution for Secure and Efficient Agricultural Supply Chain Systems
summary: The agricultural supply chain forms the backbone for feeding the world and supporting economies, but there is always a challenge to it such as traceability, inefficiencies, fraud risk, and poor transparency. Trust is hampered as many traditional systems still depend on manual procedures and distributed data records. So as to overcome the issues and improve the security, overall effectiveness, and dependability of agricultural supply chains, this paper presents a blockchain based solution. The blockchain distributed system allows safe data sharing and provides transparency for all the parties, from farmers to consumers. The framework incorporates smart contracts to automate the agreements and perform the actions, also eliminates the third-party involvement that will accelerate the procedure for supply chain. In order to monitor and track the agricultural products in real time during harvesting, storage, transportation, and delivery, the model also incorporates Internet of Things (IoT) devices. These overall systems enhance product authenticity and traceability by directly feeding precise, timestamped data into the blockchain. The results demonstrate that integrating blockchain, smart contracts, and IoT presents a viable way to address persistent issues in the agricultural supply chain and create a more reliable and effective system for all parties.

title: Functional Positioning, Scenario Demands and Digital Transformation Paths
summary: Digitalization is reshaping urban commercial spaces. Existing research and practices, however, often take for granted that uniform technology deployment delivers comparable outcomes, while paying inadequate attention to scenario variations across districts with different functional orientations. This paper selects four representative characteristic commercial districts in Haikou—Qilou Old Street, Mission Hills Resort, cdf Haikou Riyue Square, and the South Gate Night Market of Hainan University—as cases for a multi-case comparative study. Drawing on 800 consumer questionnaires, semi-structured interviews with 24 merchants, 30 days of on-site observation, and publicly available literature, it analyzes functional positioning, scenario demands, merchant capabilities and collaboration mechanisms. The findings indicate that mobile payment adoption ranges from 92% to 99% across the four districts, but platform awareness and sustained usage have not risen in tandem, creating a technology-application gap. Historical-cultural districts, culture-tourism integrated districts, commercial complexes and nighttime convenience districts center their core demands on cultural revitalization, cross-format synergy, shopping decision efficiency and instant turnover respectively. Inadequate digital literacy among merchants and insufficient collaborative support act as shared constraints, yet they operate through markedly different mechanisms. Accordingly, this paper proposes a layered "common foundation – classified application" pathway, offering a scenario-based analytical framework for the digital transformation of diversified commercial spaces in tourist cities.

title: The relationship between corporate governance mechanisms and carbon emissions performance in advanced and emerging economies
summary: This study investigates how corporate governance attributes shape firms’ carbon emissions performance, with the aim of identifying internal governance mechanisms that support effective carbon management and highlighting governance gaps that may impede such performance. The study uses a balanced panel of 972 listed non-financial firms from the world’s five largest economies—the United States, China, Germany, Japan, and India- over the period 2020–2024. The analysis utilises multiple econometric approaches, including fixed effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, Pooled Ordinary Least Squares (POLS) with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and industry, year and country dummies, and 2 SLS estimation to address potential endogeneity. Our results indicate that boards characterised by greater gender diversity and independence, and that meet more frequently are associated with lower carbon emissions intensity and improved carbon emissions performance. CEO non-duality is also associated with improved carbon emissions performance. However, board size does not appear to improve such performance. This study provides novel cross-country evidence on the governance–carbon emissions association using firm-level data from five major economies. It advances the literature by offering robust insights into how board structures influence corporate carbon mitigation within an international institutional setting.

title: Public sector corporate governance revisited: the ROI's non-commercial semi-state sector
summary: In May 2009, the Republic of Ireland’s (ROI) Code of Practice for the Governance of State Bodies came into effect. In addition to imposing further compliance and reporting obligations on the boards of the ROI’s statutory agencies, the Code more ciearly defined the role and responsibilities of board members. A review of the national and international literature indicated that although the significance of boards was generally accepted, agreement as to the attributes that deliver and/or determine their effectiveness was lacking. Furthermore, it was observed that despite voluminous research on the boards of the private sector, there was a parallel lack of focus on the boards of the public sector. Premised, primarily on the ramifications of agency theory, with little evidence of any attempt to consolidate approaches to research, the extant literature was identified as fragmented and inconsistent. This issue was adjudged to be compounded in the ROI context, where public sector agentification was revealed as unique, particularly relative to its administrative culture and the limited span of control of its agencies, a sector which distinguishes between its commercial and non-commercial wings. This suggested that research into the ROI’s agencies and its governance was warranted. The review further indicated that despite the considerable body of literature on codes of governance practice, few studies had systematically analysed the impact of codes on corporate structures or the behaviours of board directors and none had done so within a public sector framework. Critics of mainstream governance research were observed to comment that an understanding of non-profit boards that was premised on the normative literature was far too simplistic. It was argued that as a consequence, nonprofit, and in particular public sector, governance was inadequately theorised, researched and understood. In response, this thesis set out to explore whether a series of board demographic, board practice and board structure variables, identified in the public sector literature as determinants of board effectiveness, would be significant in the ROI’s Non-Commercial Semi State Bodies (NCSSBs). The research was undertaken to establish a baseline of data on the sector’s governance across a range of indicators. The study was carried out by means of a board governance questionnaire conducted amongst a purposeful sample of NCSSBs, consisting of 16 boards and 149 board members. The empirical analysis of the hypotheses developed from the theoretical framework presented indicates mixed findings: where no relationships of significance between the board member demographics variables and board effectiveness are identified while, some evidence in support of statistically significant associations between certain of the board practice and board structure variables were revealed. Relative to the Code of Practice implementation indicators, the results suggest significant relationships between two of the three variables tested, namely board size and relationship with parent department, while no association was observed with the method of board member appointment variables. The findings for the descriptive analyses reveal some interesting results, key of which are indications that the sector’s board members emerge from a select coterie of Irish society and that board training and orientation uptake is at odds with participants reported governance awareness levels. The findings indicate that as only certain of the attributes of board effectiveness are manifest in the sample boards, their effectiveness will not be optimum as theorised by the relevant public sector literature. It is posited, that other factors unexplored by this research are at play which may present a basis for future research. This study contributes to our understanding of public sector board effectiveness relative to research approaches that treat of board effectiveness from nuanced and context sensitive perspectives. It is anticipated that the results of this study will stimulate future research, which might explore, in particular, the anomalies revealed by this sample’s unique demographic profile.
